key: the street map that shows which photo
name: ch00_photos_vs_street_map
alt: A student surrounded by loose street photographs, then the same photos pinned onto a big city map that shows how they connect.
scene: A wide two-part scene on a single study table seen from slightly above. On the LEFT half, a young engineering student in his early twenties, grey hoodie, glasses pushed up on his forehead, sits frowning at a messy fan of about a dozen sharp photographs of Indian city streets: a lane of a vegetable market, a flyover, a temple corner, a bus stop, a row of shops with awnings. Each photo is crisp, but they lie at random angles with no lines between them, and a small question-mark cloud floats over his head. On the RIGHT half, the same photographs are now pinned onto a large unfolded paper street map of the same city; thin red threads run from each photo to its exact spot on the map, and the roads between them are visible, so you can trace a route from the market lane to the flyover to the bus stop. The student, now smiling, points with a pencil at one pinned photo of the temple corner, ready to zoom in on it with a magnifying glass resting beside the map. A steel tumbler of tea and a highlighter sit on the table. Warm evening desk-lamp light, calm and focused mood. Labels: "PAPERS" on a small tag beside the loose photos on the left, "THE BOOK" in the top corner of the map on the right.

key: The shortcut is only useful because
name: ch00_doctor_shorthand
alt: Two doctors in a hospital corridor understand a short code instantly, while a confused visitor sees the long meaning hidden behind it.
scene: A bright hospital corridor in an Indian city hospital, seen at eye level. In the foreground LEFT, two doctors stand facing each other: a woman in her forties with a white coat, stethoscope around her neck and a clipboard, and a younger male doctor in green scrubs, nodding quickly. A speech bubble from the woman contains only the two big letters "MI". Above both doctors floats a large shared thought bubble that unpacks the shortcut into a small clear drawing: a heart with one artery pinched off and a darkened patch of muscle, showing that both of them see the full meaning behind the two letters. In the RIGHT background, a middle-aged visitor in a plain kurta holding a tiffin box and a file of reports stands near a bench, overhearing; above his head the same "MI" appears with a big question mark and no picture behind it. A thin dotted line runs from the shared thought bubble toward a closed book lying on the bench next to the visitor, as if the book is the key that would let him see the heart drawing too. Clean daylight from tall windows, a wall clock, a hand-sanitiser stand, calm but busy mood. Label: "SHORTCUT" on a small tag under the "MI" bubble.

key: Two dials on every database
name: ch00_two_dials
alt: A control panel with two big dials, one for storage and one for distribution, with product cards showing different dial settings.
scene: A close, straight-on view of a sturdy metal control panel mounted on a workshop wall, like the panel of an old water pump or a radio station console. Two large round dials sit side by side, each with a chunky pointer knob. The LEFT dial has a curved scale running from a small tree-shaped icon at one end to a stacked-layers icon at the other end, and its pointer rests near the tree end. The RIGHT dial has a longer scale with four small icons in order: a single box, a box with two smaller boxes hanging off it, three boxes in a voting circle, and three boxes in a loose triangle with no centre; its pointer sits on the second icon. Below the panel, a technician in her thirties, navy overalls, hair tied back, holds up a small product card with a tiny printed sketch of the same two dials set to particular positions, comparing it to the real panel. Pinned along the panel's edge, three other product cards show the dials set in different positions, making the point that each product is just one combination of the two settings. Even workshop light, neutral, explanatory mood. Labels: "STORAGE" engraved above the left dial, "DISTRIBUTION" engraved above the right dial.

key: into an alphabetical folder as it
name: ch01_shoebox_vs_folders
alt: One person tosses receipts into a shoebox and struggles on tax day; another files each receipt into labelled folders and finds one instantly.
scene: A split-panel scene divided by a thin vertical line, both halves set in small Indian home offices on the evening of tax day, a wall calendar with a date circled in red in each. LEFT panel: a man in his thirties in a vest and lungi sits cross-legged on the floor with an overturned cardboard shoebox, hundreds of crumpled receipts spread around him like snow; he sorts them into rough piles with a tired, sweaty face, a ceiling fan spinning above, a cold cup of tea forgotten. A small inset at the top shows his everyday habit: one quick flick of a receipt into the open box, with a lightning symbol for speed. RIGHT panel: a woman of similar age in a cotton salwar suit stands at a steel cupboard with a row of neatly labelled alphabetical folders; she calmly pulls out exactly one folder with two fingers and the receipt she needs is on top. Her inset at the top shows her everyday habit: carefully filing one receipt into the correct folder, with a small clock icon showing it takes a little longer each time. Soft lamplight, gentle humour, neither side shown as the winner. Labels: "WRITE FAST" over the left inset, "READ FAST" over the right inset.

key: The waiter (transport) takes the order
name: ch01_restaurant_dbms_parts
alt: A cutaway of a restaurant where waiter, head chef, line cooks and a well-organised pantry stand for the parts of a database system.
scene: A cutaway view of a busy Indian restaurant drawn like a doll's house, read left to right. Far LEFT, at the dining area, a young waiter in a black waistcoat takes an order on a notepad from a family at a table, while a corded phone on his podium connects by a dotted line to a sign reading "branch 2". Next, at a high pass counter, the head chef, a stout man in his fifties with a tall white hat, reads the order slip, checks a small permission list, and writes a numbered cooking plan on a chalkboard. In the middle, three line cooks in aprons work at burners following the chalkboard; one of them reaches through a hatch into the next-door branch's kitchen to borrow a bowl of paneer. On the RIGHT is the pantry, drawn larger with five details: a pantry manager holding a ring of fridge keys, a schedule board so two dishes do not grab the same tray, labelled shelves of ingredients, a small counter where the most-used spices sit within arm's reach, and a thick logbook on a hook next to a battery lamp for restocking after a power cut. Warm kitchen light, steam, purposeful bustle. Labels: "QUERY PROCESSOR" above the head chef, "EXECUTION" above the line cooks, "STORAGE ENGINE" above the pantry.

key: Every sale you also jot in a notebook
name: ch01_shopkeeper_ledger_notebook
alt: A shopkeeper keeps stock in his head, jots each sale in a notebook, copies totals to a ledger each evening, and recovers from both after fainting.
scene: A three-step strip of panels set in a small Indian kirana shop with shelves of rice sacks, biscuit packets and oil tins. Panel ONE, daytime: the shopkeeper, a cheerful man in his fifties with a moustache, white half-sleeve shirt and a pen behind his ear, hands a packet of biscuits to a schoolgirl; a thought bubble over his head holds tiny stock counts, and with his other hand he is already jotting the sale in a small spiral notebook on the counter before saying done. Panel TWO, evening: under a single bulb he copies totals from the notebook into a thick red cloth-bound ledger, and tears out the used notebook pages into a waste basket; a wall clock shows nine o'clock. Panel THREE, next morning: the shopkeeper sits dazed on a stool with a cartoon swirl over his head, his thought bubble empty, while his son in a T-shirt opens the red ledger at last night's page and reads only the few fresh notebook pages written since, a curved arrow showing ledger plus pages giving back the full stock count. Warm, homely, slightly comic mood. Labels: "LOG" on the spiral notebook, "CHECKPOINT" on the red ledger.

key: stack of filled-in sign-up forms
name: ch01_signup_forms_phone_numbers
alt: A volunteer must lift and turn every whole sign-up form just to copy one phone number from each.
scene: A medium shot of a folding table at a neighbourhood sports-club registration desk, a hand-painted banner and plastic chairs in the background. A volunteer in her twenties, club T-shirt, lanyard, hair in a ponytail, works through a tall stack of filled-in paper sign-up forms. She lifts one whole form with both hands; every form is a full page with many filled boxes: a passport-size photo, name, date of birth, a long address block, blood group, emergency contact, and only one small box for the phone number, which is highlighted in yellow. With her other hand she copies that single number into a narrow notebook that already holds a neat column of numbers. Behind her, a growing pile of turned-over forms leans dangerously, and faint grey shading covers every part of each form except the highlighted phone box, showing how much paper she lifts that she does not need. A small inset bubble near the top shows a tidy alternative: a single long strip of paper containing only phone numbers, one under another. Late morning daylight, patient but slightly weary mood. Label: "ROW STORE" on a tag clipped to the stack of forms, "COLUMN" beside the inset strip.

key: A ledger with separate notebooks for
name: ch01_line_number_notebooks
alt: Three notebooks for symbol, date and price lie side by side, and a ruler across line 3 shows the same trade in each.
scene: A top-down view of a wooden desk in a small trading office. Three identical slim notebooks lie open side by side, each with a hand-written title on its cover flap: one holds only stock symbols written as short made-up codes, one only dates, one only prices with rupee-free numbers like 412.50. Every notebook has the same ruled lines with the same printed line numbers in the left margin, and the entries are written in the same order in all three. A long transparent ruler rests across all three notebooks at line 3, and a gentle yellow glow highlights the three entries on that line, which together form one complete trade. A clerk's hand, with a steel watch on the wrist, holds the ruler in place, while a small speech bubble from off-frame asks "trade 3?". In the margins nothing else is written; there are no ID numbers next to entries, and a small crossed-out sticky note reading "#3" sits to one side to show that an explicit ID is not needed. A cup of chai and a calculator sit at the edge. Clean morning light, orderly and calm mood. Label: "LINE = ID" on the ruler.

key: Counting the coins in a jar where coins
name: ch01_coin_jar_vs_tray
alt: Coins mixed with buttons and keys in a jar are slow to count, while a tray of only coins tips into a counting machine and can be summarised.
scene: A split-panel scene on a shop counter, divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a teenage boy in a school uniform sits hunched over a glass jar tipped onto the counter; coins are mixed with shirt buttons, crumpled receipts, a bunch of keys and rubber bands, and he picks out one coin at a time with tweezers-like fingers, a slow tally written on his palm, a frustrated face. RIGHT panel: a woman shopkeeper in her forties wearing a printed saree slides a long shallow tray filled only with identical silver five-rupee-sized coins, standing upright in neat rows, into the mouth of a grey coin-counting machine; a whole row disappears into the machine at once, with motion lines and a small counter display. Next to the tray, a single small paper chit replaces the long list of coins, reading "400 × 5", with an arrow from the tray to the chit. Bright, cheerful shop lighting with a calendar and a plastic toran in the background. Labels: "SIMD" above the counting machine, "COMPRESSION" above the paper chit.

key: one drawer per column family
name: ch01_column_family_drawers
alt: A filing cabinet with one drawer per column family; one drawer is open to a folder whose sheets carry date stamps, while another drawer stays shut.
scene: A three-quarter view of a tall green steel filing cabinet in a government-style office, with three drawers each carrying a printed label card. The middle drawer is pulled open; inside, manila folders stand in strict order, each with a tab showing a website address written backwards in short form like "com.site.www". One folder is lifted half out by a clerk in his late twenties, beige shirt, sleeves rolled, reading glasses; within it, several sheets are fanned out, and each sheet carries a small stamped box in its top corner with a column name and a date, the newest dated sheet on top. The top drawer, labelled for anchors, stays firmly shut with a little padlock-free closed look and a faint cobweb, showing it is never touched for this task. A thin arrow leads from the clerk's eyes straight to the one open folder. Ceiling fan, file trays and a wall calendar in the background, steady fluorescent light, quiet orderly mood. Labels: "CONTENTS" on the open drawer's label card, "ANCHORS" on the closed drawer's label card.

key: Hashed: 26 pigeonholes by first letter
name: ch01_heap_hashed_iot
alt: Three ways to store letters: an unsorted box plus catalogue, 26 pigeonholes by first letter, and letters filed directly in alphabetical drawers.
scene: A triptych of three panels in a neighbourhood post office back room, the same postal clerk, a woman in her forties in a khaki uniform with a pen behind her ear, in each. LEFT panel: a big unsorted cardboard box of letters sits on the floor; on the desk beside it is a small wooden card catalogue, and she holds a card that reads "Mehta → 812", while a dotted arrow points from the card into the box at one specific letter. MIDDLE panel: a wooden wall of 26 pigeonholes each marked with a letter of the alphabet; she reaches straight into the M hole with confidence, but a speech bubble shows her puzzled about listing all names from M to P, with arrows having to dart into many holes. RIGHT panel: a cabinet of alphabetical card-catalogue drawers where the letters themselves are filed between the index cards; she pulls a drawer and the letter for Mehta is right there behind its card, with a small check mark. Soft daylight through barred windows, tidy, explanatory mood. Labels: "HEAP" above the left panel, "HASHED" above the middle panel, "IOT" above the right panel.

key: A clustered index is a dictionary
name: ch01_dictionary_vs_back_index
alt: In a dictionary all words starting with pa sit on neighbouring pages; in a textbook back index the entries send you to scattered pages.
scene: A split-panel scene on a library reading table, divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a college girl in a yellow kurta with a braid holds open a thick dictionary; three consecutive pages are fanned out under her thumb and every visible headword on them begins with the same two letters, glowing gently together as one tidy block. A short straight arrow loops across just those neighbouring pages. RIGHT panel: the same girl holds a thick school textbook open at its back index; the index column is alphabetical and neat, but from five neighbouring index entries long curving arrows fly out to sticky tabs scattered all over the book's edge, at the front, the middle and near the end, so she has to keep flipping back and forth, a slightly exasperated look on her face, a pencil tucked behind her ear and a small notepad beside her already filling with page numbers she has to chase. Wooden table, green reading lamp, a stack of books and a water bottle, warm quiet library light. Labels: "CLUSTERED" at the top of the left panel, "NONCLUSTERED" at the top of the right panel.

key: when someone moves, every card that
name: ch01_contacts_mum_lookup
alt: Three ways of finding a friend who moved: addresses on every card, cards that say ask Mum, and a card with both.
scene: A triptych of three panels, each showing a young man in his twenties in a striped T-shirt trying to visit his friend Ravi, who has just moved house. LEFT panel: on a table lie six contact cards, each with Ravi's old address written on it; a pen is busy crossing out and rewriting the address on every one of them, with a small pile-up of tired arrows. MIDDLE panel: each card only has a tiny drawing of a phone and the words "ask Mum"; the young man stands at a gate making a phone call to his mother, a smiling woman in her fifties shown in a small inset bubble reading from her own address book, and only that one book has the updated address. RIGHT panel: the card shows the old address and "ask Mum" as backup; he arrives at the old house, finds a To Let sign on the gate, makes a quick call to Mum, then crosses out the old address on his single card and writes the new one. Leafy residential Indian street, auto-rickshaw passing, afternoon sun. Labels: "DIRECT" above the left panel, "INDIRECT" above the middle panel, "HYBRID" above the right panel.

key: Three questions about how you handle
name: ch01_three_mail_habits
alt: Three pairs of mail habits: file once a day or immediately, rewrite a letter or clip a correction, alphabetical cabinet or arrival order.
scene: A grid of three horizontal strips in one small office, each strip split into a left and right half that show two opposite habits, with the same clerk, a young woman in a cotton kurta with a lanyard, in every cell. Top strip: on the left she drops letters into a wire tray labelled "today" and files them all at once in the evening, a moon in the window; on the right she files each letter into the cabinet the moment it arrives, a sun in the window. Middle strip: on the left she erases and rewrites a line directly on a letter with an eraser and pencil; on the right she leaves the letter untouched and staples a small yellow correction slip at the back. Bottom strip: on the left a cabinet drawer with tidy alphabetical tabs from A to Z; on the right a drawer where letters simply stand in the order they arrived, each with a small date stamp. Every half has a tiny icon so the contrast is clear at a glance. Even office light, neutral, diagram-like mood. Labels: "BUFFERING" beside the top strip, "MUTABILITY" beside the middle strip, "ORDERING" beside the bottom strip.

key: A coat hanger with everything hung
name: ch02_coat_hanger_rotation
alt: A coat hanger loaded on one end tips over; held from a point nearer the middle, the same clothes hang level.
scene: A split-panel scene in a tailor's shop, divided by a thin vertical line, with a pegboard wall and bolts of cloth in the background. LEFT panel: a long wooden hanger hangs from a hook at its very left end, and all the clothes, a heavy wool coat, two shirts, a scarf and a kurta, are bunched together on the right side; the hanger tilts steeply and the clothes are about to slide off, with small motion lines and a worried tailor, a lean man in his sixties with a measuring tape around his neck and spectacles, reaching out. RIGHT panel: the same tailor lifts the same hanger by a hook point nearer its middle, and now it hangs perfectly level, the exact same five garments spread evenly on both sides; a curved arrow shows the hook moving from the end to the middle. A small check mark appears near the level hanger. Each garment has a little paper tag with a number, and the numbers are identical in both panels, making it clear nothing was added or removed. Warm afternoon light through a shop window, calm, satisfying mood. Labels: "UNBALANCED" above the left panel, "ROTATED" above the right panel.

key: Memory is your desk; disk is a warehouse
name: ch02_desk_and_warehouse_trips
alt: A worker at a small desk sends a trolley to a huge warehouse, and a well-packed trolley brings back many useful items in one trip.
scene: A wide scene showing two places connected by a long corridor. In the LEFT foreground is a small wooden desk with room for only a few items, where an office worker in her thirties, cardigan over a cotton saree, works on a folder and glances at the clock. Stretching away on the RIGHT is a vast warehouse with towering steel racks numbered down the aisles, fading into the distance. Down the long corridor between them a porter in a blue uniform pushes a flat trolley. In a small inset at the top left, a badly organised warehouse forces him to bring back one lone box per trip, with many dotted footprints going back and forth. In the main scene, the warehouse shelves are arranged so that items used together sit side by side, and his trolley returns piled with a full, neat stack of related boxes from one shelf in a single trip, a check mark above it. The desk is visibly too small to hold the warehouse, emphasising that only trips can be improved, not the size of the desk. Soft industrial lighting in the warehouse, warm lamp light on the desk. Labels: "MEMORY" on a sign above the desk, "DISK" on a sign over the warehouse entrance.

key: Dropping the needle on a new song
name: ch02_record_player_io
alt: A record player: lifting the needle between songs wastes seconds, while letting the whole album play streams music continuously.
scene: A split-panel scene in a cosy living room with a cane chair, a wooden cabinet and a vinyl record player with a transparent lid, divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: an elderly man in his seventies, white kurta and shawl, keeps lifting the tone arm and dropping the needle on different tracks; dashed arcs show the arm jumping between grooves at random, a small hourglass beside each jump, and only short bursts of music notes come out between long silent gaps. His face is impatient, a half-eaten plate of biscuits forgotten at his elbow and a stack of record sleeves toppling beside him. RIGHT panel: his granddaughter, about twelve, in a school sweater, has set the needle down once at the start of the record and now sits back reading a comic, while a steady, unbroken ribbon of music notes flows out of the speaker and the needle traces one smooth spiral path across the record. A tiny hourglass appears only at the very start of her ribbon. Warm evening lamp light, nostalgic, gentle mood. Labels: "RANDOM I/O" above the left panel, "SEQUENTIAL I/O" above the right panel.

key: may only tear out whole chapters
name: ch02_pen_notebook_tear_chapter
alt: In a pen notebook lines are rewritten and crossed out; a mostly crossed-out chapter has its few good lines copied forward and is torn out.
scene: A close top-down view of a thick spiral notebook on a hostel study desk, written entirely in blue ink pen. The notebook is clearly divided into chapters by coloured tab dividers. In one early chapter, almost every line is struck through with a single neat line, and only three lines remain un-crossed, each with a small green tick. A student's hand, wrist with a thread bracelet, is copying those three good lines onto the next blank lines at the very end of the notebook, with curved arrows from each original line to its new copy. In the second half of the scene, the same hand tears that whole mostly crossed-out chapter out along the spiral, the pages coming away together in one bundle and dropping into a small wastepaper basket. There is no eraser anywhere on the desk; a pen cap and an empty eraser-shaped outline with a cross through it make clear erasing is not allowed. Desk lamp light, a laptop edge and a steel water bottle at the side, focused, tidy mood. Labels: "FULL" on a small sticky note on the notebook cover, "GARBAGE COLLECTION" above the torn-out bundle.

key: A family tree drawn on index cards
name: ch02_family_tree_cards
alt: Tracing a family line through scattered single cards takes many pulls; cards that glue three generations together need a third as many.
scene: A split-panel scene on a dining table at a family gathering, divided by a thin vertical line, both halves showing a grey-haired grandmother in a cotton saree and her teenage grandson tracing their family line. LEFT panel: a shoebox is full of loose index cards, each with a single person's small portrait sketch and name; the grandson pulls cards one at a time, and a chain of seven separate cards is laid out in a long line with arrows from each to the next, with many hand-reaching motions drawn around the box. RIGHT panel: the cards have been glued in trios, each larger card holding a grandparent, a parent and a child joined by short branch lines; the same family line now needs only three of these bigger cards, laid out with arrows between them, and the grandson holds just one more card while the grandmother smiles and points. Plates of sweets and a steel water jug on the table, warm festival lighting with marigold strings in the background. Labels: "ONE PER CARD" above the left panel, "THREE PER CARD" above the right panel.

key: A town named exactly 40 takes the third
name: ch02_junction_road_signs
alt: A roundabout with exit signs for number ranges, and a car for town 40 taking the third exit because ranges include their lower boundary.
scene: A high aerial view of a large roundabout on an Indian highway, with four exits fanning out, lined with trees and a few roadside dhabas. At the entry, a big green road sign shows four arrows with ranges: first exit "below 20", second exit "20–39", third exit "40–59", straight on "60+". On the roundabout, a small white hatchback car carries a cardboard placard on its roof with the number "40", and a dotted path traces its route past the first and second exits and out through the third exit. In a little speech bubble at the third exit, a traffic policeman in a khaki uniform and white gloves gives a thumbs up. A small inset magnifies the sign's third line to show that the range starts exactly at 40, with a tiny bracket at the start of the range. Other cars with numbers like 12, 33 and 75 take their own exits along faint dotted paths. A tea stall at the corner, a bus waiting at the second exit and a row of neem trees fill the background. Bright midday sun, clear and orderly mood. Label: "SEPARATOR KEYS" on a small banner across the top of the big sign.

key: Zooming into a map: country
name: ch02_zoom_map_then_walk
alt: Four zoom levels from country to street, each one page read, followed by a walk along the street from door to door.
scene: A staircase-like sequence of four map cards descending from the top left toward the bottom right, each card a closer zoom than the one above, joined by magnifying-glass arrows that only point downward. The first card shows the outline of a country, the second one state with a circled city, the third a city map with one neighbourhood circled, the fourth a single street with a row of numbered house doors. A small book-page icon sits on each arrow to show each zoom costs one page read, and there are no arrows going back up. At the bottom right, the street card opens into a full scene: a cheerful postman in his forties in khaki uniform with a shoulder bag walks along the street, door to door, delivering letters to houses 14, 15, 16, 17 in order, with short curved arrows linking each house to the next neighbour. Morning light, colourful houses with balconies and potted tulsi plants, steady purposeful mood. Labels: "ROOT" beside the country card, "LEAF" beside the street card, "RANGE SCAN" along the postman's path.

key: Two half-empty drawers side by side
name: ch02_merge_half_empty_drawers
alt: Cards from a half-empty drawer are poured into its neighbour, the empty drawer is thrown away, and its label is peeled off the cabinet.
scene: A three-step scene in a library catalogue room with wooden card cabinets, the same librarian in all steps: a woman in her fifties with silver-rimmed glasses on a chain, cardigan over a printed saree. Step ONE: two neighbouring drawers are pulled out side by side, each only half full of index cards, with lots of empty space visible. Step TWO: she tips the right drawer and pours its cards into the empty back half of the left drawer, a curved arrow showing the movement, cards fluttering. Step THREE: she drops the now-empty right drawer into a recycling bin and, with her other hand, peels a small label card off the cabinet front, the label curling as it comes away. A small inset bubble in the corner shows the bigger version of the same move: two half-empty cabinets being combined, and this time the peeled label is placed inside the merged cabinet between its two halves instead of being thrown away, marked with a small arrow. Warm wooden tones, filtered daylight, quiet efficient mood. Label: "MERGE" above step two.

key: get a sealed box of bytes back
name: ch03_library_helper_vs_sealed_box
alt: In a library a helper hands you any book you point at; at a warehouse you get a sealed box and must unpack it using its packing list.
scene: A split-panel scene divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a bright public library; a reader in her twenties in a denim jacket points casually at a book on a high shelf, and a friendly helper in a library apron, a young man with a lanyard, has already pulled that exact book down and is handing it to her open at the right page, with a small sparkle of ease. RIGHT panel: a grey warehouse service window with a steel counter; the same reader hands a printed slip through the window reading "aisle 7, shelf 3, 8 KB". A burly storekeeper in a vest and a cap slides back a sealed brown cardboard box taped shut, with no label except a folded paper packing list taped on top. In the foreground she has opened the box on the counter with a box-cutter and is unpacking small numbered compartments one by one, following the packing list with her finger, item by item in the listed order. The warehouse background shows endless identical sealed boxes on racks. Soft daylight on the left, flat tube light on the right, contrast between effortless and hands-on. Labels: "MEMORY" above the left panel, "DISK" above the right panel, "FILE FORMAT" on the packing list.

key: a suitcase with fixed compartments
name: ch03_suitcase_fixed_compartments
alt: A suitcase with fixed compartments and a lid note listing what sits where and how long the shirt is.
scene: A top-down view of an open hard-shell suitcase lying on a bed in an Indian home, ready for a train journey; a printed bedsheet and a ticket envelope are visible around it. The inside of the suitcase is divided by stitched fabric walls into fixed compartments that clearly cannot be resized: a small square compartment holding rolled socks, a long narrow compartment holding a folded shirt, and a few more empty compartments of fixed sizes. A young man in his twenties, kurta and jeans, leans over the suitcase writing with a marker on a white strip of tape stuck inside the lid. His note says, in two short lines, "socks: 1, 4 cm" and "shirt: 2, see tag". A tag hangs off the folded shirt with a small length written on it, and a dotted arrow links the lid note to the tag. A small crossed-out sketch near the edge shows someone trying to stretch a compartment wall, which tears, to emphasise the sizes are fixed once sewn. Warm late-afternoon window light, preparation mood, a steel tiffin carrier waiting by the door. Label: "SCHEMA" above the note on the lid.

key: A Pascal string is a parcel with
name: ch03_parcel_vs_scroll_string
alt: A parcel shows its weight on the label before opening; a scroll only reveals its length after it is unrolled to the end.
scene: A split-panel scene on a long wooden post-office counter, divided by a thin vertical line, with the same postal clerk, a young woman in a khaki saree uniform, in both halves. LEFT panel: she holds a neatly wrapped brown parcel and simply reads the label, where a clear box shows the weight "2.4 kg"; a small check mark and a tiny clock showing almost no time spent float beside her, and the parcel is still sealed. RIGHT panel: she has a long rolled paper scroll tied with red string; she unrolls it along the entire counter and off the edge onto the floor, walking backward to follow it, until she finally reaches a small dark full-stop mark at the very end; only then does she write the length on a notepad. A long dotted arrow runs the whole length of the scroll to show she had to travel to the end before knowing its size. The background has wooden pigeonholes, rubber stamps and a wall clock. Bright, warm daylight, light humour. Labels: "LENGTH FIRST" above the left panel, "NULL-TERMINATED" above the right panel.

key: An enum is a dial with a few positions
name: ch03_enum_dial_vs_flag_switches
alt: A rotary dial that points to only one position at a time beside a plate of eight switches where any combination can be on.
scene: A close, straight-on view of an Indian household wall with two controls mounted side by side on a pale yellow painted surface. On the LEFT, a chunky round rotary dial like an old fan regulator, with five numbered positions around its edge; its pointer sits on position 3, and the other positions are dimmed, and a curved arrow shows that turning it to any new position means leaving the old one, so only one number is ever lit. On the RIGHT, a long white modular switch plate with eight small rocker switches in a row; switches 1, 3, 4 and 7 are flipped on with little orange indicator dots glowing, the rest are off, and a tiny row of matching ones and zeros sits printed under the switches. A woman in her thirties in a house kurta reaches up with one finger to flip switch 6 on, with no effect on any other switch. Above the plate, a ceiling fan and two bulbs connected by thin wires show that several things can be on at once. Warm morning light, homely, clear mood. Labels: "ENUM" above the dial, "FLAGS" above the switch plate.

key: the trailer is the index at the back
name: ch03_book_header_pages_trailer
alt: A book whose title page acts as the header, equal-size pages, and an index at the back as the trailer, with page 100 opened directly.
scene: A three-quarter view of a thick hardcover book lying on a desk, shown in an exploded, fanned-out way so its parts are clear. At the front, the title page and table of contents are pulled slightly forward and glow softly. In the middle, the pages are fanned like a deck of cards, every page exactly the same size with an identical outline, and a few page numbers visible at their corners. At the back, the index pages are pulled slightly out, with alphabetical entries. A student's hand, wearing a red thread on the wrist, slides a ruler alongside the closed edge of the book and lands precisely at a page with a bookmark marked "100", opening it at once without counting from the start; a small calculation bubble shows a simple multiplication of page size times 100 leading straight to the spot. A pencil, an eraser and a cup of filter coffee sit beside the book. Soft desk-lamp light, studious and tidy mood. Labels: "HEADER" pointing to the title page, "PAGES" across the fanned middle, "TRAILER" pointing to the index at the back.

key: always in the same spot on the label
name: ch03_shipping_label_fixed_fields
alt: A parcel scanner reads fixed boxes in the same spot on every label, while the parcels behind the labels are all different sizes.
scene: A medium-wide shot of a courier sorting hub with a moving conveyor belt. Parcels of very different sizes ride along the belt: a tiny envelope-sized pouch, a medium cardboard box, a long tube and a big flat carton. Every parcel carries an identical white label in its top-left corner with the same grid of small fixed boxes in the same positions, including boxes printed with "weight", "length" and "flags", and a red laser line from an overhead scanner hits exactly the same spot on each label. A sorter in his twenties, high-visibility vest over a T-shirt, cap turned backward, watches the scanner screen, which shows matching fields read from each parcel, while a small arrow from the "length" box on one label points to the actual size of its parcel. The parcels themselves are visibly mismatched in size, but the labels never move. Bright industrial overhead lighting, a busy but orderly mood, stacks of sacks and roll cages in the background. Label: "FIXED HEADER" on a tag hanging above the scanner, "VARIABLE DATA" painted on the side of the belt.

key: Best fit hunts for the tightest bay
name: ch03_car_park_first_best_fit
alt: A car park after some cars leave: one car takes the first gap it sees, another hunts for the tightest bay, and the lot is later re-parked bumper to bumper.
scene: A triptych of three aerial views of the same small open-air car park beside a market, painted bays of mixed sizes, gaps left where cars have driven away. LEFT panel: a small red hatchback has pulled straight into the very first empty space near the entrance, which is a long bus bay; it sits at one end and leaves an awkward half-bay gap behind it, highlighted with a hatched outline. MIDDLE panel: a similar car drives a dotted route past several gaps to find the one space that fits it almost exactly, an attendant in a cap guiding with a whistle and pointing. RIGHT panel: a sign at the entrance says "closed 5 min"; two attendants wave cars forward, and all the cars are now parked bumper to bumper on one side, leaving one big clean empty block at the far end, with arrows showing each car's short move. Scattered neem trees and a sugarcane-juice cart at the edge, bright afternoon sun, practical, slightly busy mood. Labels: "FIRST FIT" above the left panel, "BEST FIT" above the middle panel, "DEFRAGMENT" above the right panel.

key: written on the envelope (file name)
name: ch03_document_language_hints
alt: Three ways to learn a document's language before reading: the envelope, a cover note, or a first line everyone can read, then picking the right dictionary.
scene: A wide scene of a translation desk in a busy office, where a translator in his forties, half-sleeve checked shirt, reading glasses on his nose, receives three different documents. In the LEFT foreground, a sealed envelope has the language written in small letters in the corner of its front, and he is glancing at it. In the MIDDLE, a document comes with a separate small cover note clipped to it, which states its language. On the RIGHT, an opened document whose very first line is in plain simple English, followed by lines in a script he cannot yet read. Behind him, a wooden shelf holds a row of thick dictionaries with different coloured spines for Hindi, Tamil, Bengali, French and more. A dotted arrow from each of the three hints leads to the matching dictionary on the shelf, and he is reaching for one of them before reading any further. Steady office light, a ceiling fan, files stacked high, focused, methodical mood. Labels: "FILE NAME" by the envelope, "SIDECAR FILE" by the cover note, "HEADER" by the first line of the open document.

key: Each page begins with the same stamp
name: ch04_magic_stamp_pages
alt: Every page in a stack starts with the same stamp; a reader who opens in the middle of a page sees no stamp and stops before trusting the numbers.
scene: A split-panel scene on an accountant's desk, divided by a thin vertical line, with the same young auditor, a woman in her late twenties with a neat bun, white shirt and a lanyard, in both halves. In both panels a tall stack of loose ledger pages lies before her, and every page begins with an identical round purple rubber stamp in its top-left corner, the same shape and colour each time. LEFT panel: she lifts a page cleanly from the top of the stack; her eye lands first on the purple stamp, a small green tick floats beside it, and she begins reading the columns of numbers below with confidence. RIGHT panel: she has accidentally pulled a sheet that was torn across the middle, so she is looking at the lower half of a page with no stamp at its top; she stops with her pen raised, a red warning triangle and a question mark beside the missing stamp, and the numbers below are faded out to show she will not trust them yet. A rubber stamp and ink pad sit beside the stack. Even office light, careful, cautious mood. Labels: "MAGIC NUMBER" next to the stamp on the left, "WRONG OFFSET" above the right panel.

key: With sibling links, you walk next door
name: ch04_sibling_links_street
alt: With sibling links you walk next door; without them you walk back to the junction and main road, then down the next block to reach the neighbouring house.
scene: An aerial illustrated map of an Indian residential colony with a main road at the top, two side roads branching down from junctions, and a row of small colourful houses along each side road. The last house on the first block and the first house on the next block sit back to back across a short garden wall. Two routes are drawn from the same last house, where a young delivery boy in a red T-shirt with a cycle and a parcel stands. A short green arrow goes straight from his house through a small gate in the wall to the neighbouring first house of the next block, a few steps only. A long red dotted path goes the other way: back up the first side road to its junction, up again to the main road, along the main road to the next junction, then down the next side road to the same house, with tiny footstep marks and a sweating face icon at the corner. Small street lamps, a temple at the main road corner, a vegetable cart and a cow on the main road. Bright morning light, clear, map-like mood. Labels: "SIBLING LINK" beside the green arrow, "VIA PARENT" beside the red route.

key: If you arrive at 7 pm, the first shop
name: ch04_last_entry_signs
alt: Two neighbouring shops at 7 pm: one with an open-ended sign lets a customer in to search for nothing, the other's sign sends him next door.
scene: A split-panel evening street scene in an Indian market lane, divided by a thin vertical line, with the same customer, a man in his thirties in a checked shirt carrying a cloth shopping bag, in both halves. A lamp-post clock in each panel shows seven o'clock. LEFT panel: a small shop with a hand-written sign on the door reading "last entry: anytime"; the customer has gone inside and is searching row after row of empty shelves with a torch, his shadow long on the floor, finding nothing, with a sweat drop and a question mark above him. RIGHT panel: a neighbouring shop with a printed sign on the door reading "last entry: 6 pm"; the customer stands outside, reads the sign at a glance and turns toward the brightly lit shop next door, with a curved arrow pointing him there and a small light-bulb of realisation above his head. Shuttered stalls, a tea vendor with a kettle, string lights coming on, dusky blue sky. Gently comic, clear mood. Labels: "NO HIGH KEY" above the left panel, "HIGH KEY" above the right panel.

key: the books are shelved in the order they
name: ch04_catalogue_trip_per_compare
alt: A librarian checks a sorted card catalogue but must walk to a far shelf after every card to read a spine before deciding where to look next.
scene: A wide interior of an old college library. In the LEFT foreground, a tall wooden card catalogue cabinet with alphabetical drawers; one drawer is open in the middle and a librarian in his fifties, cardigan over a shirt, spectacles, holds up one card. On the RIGHT and stretching into the background, long shelves of books whose spines are visibly not in alphabetical order: each book has a small arrival-date sticker, and colours and sizes are mixed. A dotted footpath loops from the catalogue to a particular shelf far away, where the librarian is drawn again reading a spine, then back to the catalogue, where he flips to an earlier card, then out again to another distant shelf. Each round trip is numbered with a small circle, 1, 2, 3, and each loop is long, with tiny footstep marks along the floor. At the far shelf, a speech bubble shows him thinking "earlier" with a left-pointing arrow. Dust motes in shafts of afternoon light from tall windows, quiet, tiring mood. Labels: "SORTED" on the catalogue, "UNSORTED" over the shelves.

key: That reprint is the hidden cost of
name: ch04_badge_reprint_parent_pointer
alt: After a team splits in two, HR must reprint the manager badges of everyone who moved to the new team.
scene: A wide shot of an open-plan Indian tech office during a team reorganisation. On the LEFT, a desk with a badge printer churning out a long line of plastic ID cards, and an HR executive in her thirties in a smart kurta and lanyard feeding blank cards in with a slightly harried expression, a stack of printed badges growing beside her. In the CENTRE, a big whiteboard shows a team chart split into two by a red marker line, with one manager's name at the top of each half and an arrow showing half the people moving to the new team. On the RIGHT, a queue of five employees from the moved half, a mix of ages and clothing, stand holding out their old badges, each showing a small manager line, while one of them is already clipping on a freshly printed badge with a new manager line. The employees who stayed on the old team sit at their desks in the background, badges unchanged, working calmly. A small sticky note on the printer reads "reprint". Bright office lighting, plants and laptops, mildly busy and wry mood. Label: "PARENT POINTER" on a small banner above the badge printer.

key: repack the two into three boxes
name: ch04_book_boxes_split_rebalance
alt: Three ways to pack books when a box is full: open a new half-full box, slide books into a neighbour, or repack two full boxes into three two-thirds-full boxes.
scene: A triptych of three panels in a room full of cardboard boxes during a house move, the same mover in each: a sturdy man in his thirties in a vest and towel over his shoulder. LEFT panel: one box overflows with books; he opens a new empty box beside it and moves half the books in, leaving two boxes each half full, gaps visible at the top of both. MIDDLE panel: the overflowing box sits next to a neighbour box that has room; he slides a few books sideways from the full box into the neighbour, a short arrow, no new box needed. RIGHT panel: two neighbouring boxes are both completely full; he has unpacked them and is repacking the books into three boxes, each filled about two-thirds, with a small tired-looking sweat drop and a bigger stack of lifted books in his arms, showing more effort. Faint fill lines drawn on the side of each box make the fullness easy to compare. Late afternoon sun through bare windows, rolled carpets and a steel trunk in the background, busy moving-day mood. Labels: "SPLIT" above the left panel, "REBALANCE" above the middle panel, "B* SPLIT" above the right panel.

key: Quickbalance just turns to a fresh page
name: ch04_ledger_quickbalance_fastpath
alt: A normal split leaves a trail of half-empty ledger pages behind, while quickbalance leaves full pages full and simply turns to a fresh page with a finger kept on the end.
scene: A split-panel view of two thick bound account ledgers lying open on a shop counter, divided by a thin vertical line, entries always added at the end in date order. LEFT panel: the ledger's earlier pages are each only half filled, their lower halves blank, because every time the last page filled it was torn in half and the bottom half carried forward; a row of small torn-edge marks and pale empty halves runs back through the book, and a cobweb sits on the oldest half-empty page, showing nobody will ever write in the past again. RIGHT panel: the ledger's earlier pages are all completely full of neat entries, and the accountant, an older man in a white dhoti and spectacles, has simply turned to a fresh clean page at the end; his left index finger stays resting on the final page with a small bookmark ribbon, while a ghosted dotted arrow from the front cover of the book is crossed out, showing he never starts searching from the front. A brass oil lamp and an abacus sit beside the books. Warm lamp light, tidy and efficient mood. Labels: "SPLIT" above the left panel, "QUICKBALANCE" above the right panel, "FASTPATH" beside the resting finger.

key: you fill drawer after drawer in order
name: ch04_bulk_load_cabinet
alt: A clerk fills cabinet drawers one after another from an already sorted pile and writes each drawer's first label on an index card.
scene: A medium shot of a records room with a tall empty steel filing cabinet of six drawers. In the LEFT foreground, a perfectly sorted pile of paper files stands on a trolley, each file tab showing an increasing number from top to bottom. A young clerk in her twenties, cotton saree with a cardigan and a pen clipped to it, lifts the next block of files in order and drops them straight into the open drawer, which is filling neatly to the front. The drawers above are already full and closed, filled in sequence from top to bottom with small numbers one, two, three painted on their fronts, and the drawers below are still empty. Taped to the side of the cabinet is an index card listing just the first file number of each completed drawer, and she is writing the next entry with her free hand. A crossed-out inset bubble in the top corner shows the slow alternative: someone inserting a single file into the middle of a crammed drawer and shuffling everything. Clean daylight through a barred window, calm, efficient mood. Label: "BULK LOAD" on a tag on the trolley.

key: Vacuum-packing clothes to fit more
name: ch04_vacuum_bags_airline
alt: Vacuum-packed clothes still cost whole bags at check-in: a half-bag pack costs one bag, a slightly oversized pack costs two, and clothes must be unpacked before wearing.
scene: A wide scene at an airport check-in counter with a weighing belt. In the CENTRE, a young woman in her twenties, travel hoodie and sneakers, places luggage on the belt while an airline agent in a neat blazer behind the counter points at a size frame. Three items are lined up: a vacuum-sealed clear plastic bag of clothes squeezed flat, only half the height of the size frame, sitting inside one full standard suitcase with lots of empty space around it; next, a vacuum bag slightly too long, bulging a few centimetres past the size frame, so the agent holds up two fingers and a second suitcase has to be used. A small price tag icon over each shows one bag and two bags. In a small inset bubble on the RIGHT, the same woman in a hotel room cutting open a vacuum bag, clothes puffing back to full size, before she can wear a single shirt, a small pump lying on the bed. Bright, airy terminal lighting, travel trolleys in the background, light humour. Labels: "COMPRESSION" above the first vacuum bag, "WHOLE PAGES" above the size frame.

key: The lock manager hands out keys to
name: ch05_bank_branch_components
alt: A bank branch cutaway: a floor manager with a list of open requests, a key keeper for deposit boxes, a counter where ledgers are edited, and a carbon receipt book.
scene: A cutaway view of an Indian bank branch drawn like a doll's house, read from left to right. LEFT: the floor manager, a woman in her forties in a formal saree with a name badge, stands holding a clipboard listing open customer requests, each with a tick box, while two customers wait on a bench. CENTRE-LEFT: by the vault door, a key keeper, an older man in a grey uniform, stands at a board of hanging keys for safe-deposit boxes; two customers peer into one box together with read-only looks, while a third holds the only key that lets him change the contents, a small padlock icon over him. CENTRE-RIGHT: a long counter where clerks have pulled thick red ledgers out of the vault and are editing entries. RIGHT: a clerk at a small desk writes every edit first into a carbon-copy receipt book, the blue carbon copy showing underneath, before the ledger is touched; above the whole branch the ceiling lights are shown flickering out in a small inset, with the receipt book glowing as the thing used to rebuild the ledgers. Warm tube lighting, marble floor, busy but orderly mood. Labels: "LOCK MANAGER" above the key board, "PAGE CACHE" above the counter, "LOG" above the receipt book.

key: A book on the reserve shelf is pinned
name: ch05_reading_room_ref_pin_dirty
alt: A library reading room: a book on a reader's desk is not reshelved, a reserve-shelf book stays out, and a pencil-marked book must have its notes copied before going back.
scene: A wide view of a quiet university reading room with long wooden tables, green lamps and tall windows, a library assistant in his twenties with a book trolley moving through. LEFT: a student in a hoodie reads an open book at a desk; the assistant passes with his trolley and walks right by, with a small hand-sign icon above the book showing it is in use and will not be taken. CENTRE: a glass-fronted reserve shelf behind the issue desk holds a few books with ribbon markers, nobody reading them, and a small sign says "reserve"; the assistant's trolley path curves around it without stopping. RIGHT: on the trolley itself lies a returned book with pencil notes in its margins; before it goes back to the stacks, a senior librarian in a cardigan copies those pencil notes carefully into a large master copy on a lectern, with a dotted arrow from the margins to the master. In the background, long stacks of shelves where books are being returned. Soft daylight and lamplight, hushed, careful mood. Labels: "REFERENCED" above the reader's desk, "PINNED" above the reserve shelf, "DIRTY" above the pencil-marked book.

key: you keep them torn out and taped to the
name: ch05_map_pages_on_dashboard
alt: In a car, the country and regional map pages are taped to the dashboard while street pages stay in the glovebox until needed.
scene: An interior view from the back seat of an Indian family car on a road trip, looking forward over the driver's shoulder through the windscreen at a highway with trucks and hills. Taped to the dashboard in front of the passenger are two worn, folded map pages, one showing the outline of the country and one showing a region, both covered in fingerprints and pencil marks from constant use. The passenger, a woman in her forties with sunglasses on her head and a dupatta, glances at them while pointing the driver ahead. The driver, her husband in a half-sleeve shirt, keeps his eyes on the road. In the foreground, the glovebox is open and she is pulling out one thin street-level page from a thick map book inside; the book still has dozens of street pages folded neatly inside, each untouched. Small dotted arrows show the taped pages being used every trip, and one arrow from the glovebox showing the single street page being fetched only now. Bright afternoon light, a dangling air freshener, cheerful travel mood. Labels: "ALWAYS IN CACHE" across the dashboard pages, "ON DEMAND" beside the glovebox.

key: New arrivals wait in the lobby
name: ch05_club_doorman_2q
alt: At a club, new arrivals wait in a lobby; a doorman compares who has visited more before letting someone into the main room, and returning regulars get a VIP wristband.
scene: A wide cutaway of a busy club at night, with three zones from left to right. LEFT: a small lobby with a velvet rope where newly arrived guests, young people in party clothes, wait on a short bench; the lobby is full and one more guest squeezes in at the door. CENTRE: a burly doorman in his thirties, black T-shirt, earpiece and a clipboard, stands between the lobby and the main room; he holds up two visitor cards side by side, one from the guest leaving the lobby and one from the person at the end of a line in the main room marked with a dotted area, each card showing a small count of visits this month as tally marks. He points to the card with more tally marks, while an arrow shows the other person being walked out of the side door. RIGHT: the main room's dance floor, where a few regulars, one woman in a sequinned kurta and one man in a blazer, have fresh glowing wristbands snapped on by a staff member, and stand in a roped-off protected area. Purple and blue party lights, music notes, lively but orderly mood. Labels: "ADMISSION" above the lobby, "PROBATION" above the dotted area, "PROTECTED" above the wristband area.

key: A fuzzy checkpoint is counting shelf by
name: ch05_sync_vs_fuzzy_checkpoint
alt: One shop closes to count stock; another counts shelf by shelf while customers shop, after noting the time counting began.
scene: A split-panel scene of two similar Indian grocery stores, divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: the shutter is half down with a hand-written sign hanging on it reading "closed for stock count"; outside, three customers wait impatiently with bags, one checking his watch. Inside, two staff in aprons count tins on every shelf at once with clipboards, the aisles empty of shoppers. RIGHT panel: the shop is fully open and busy; customers with baskets browse the aisles, while one staff member, a young woman in a store T-shirt and cap, counts just one shelf of biscuit packets with a clipboard. On a whiteboard behind the counter she has written "started 9:00", and a wall clock shows 9:20. Above the right panel, a small inset shows the next morning: after an interruption, she checks only the sales slips dated after 9:00, with a short arrow from the whiteboard note to a thin stack of slips. Bright shop lighting, shelves of rice bags and oil tins, practical mood. Labels: "SYNC CHECKPOINT" above the left panel, "FUZZY CHECKPOINT" above the right panel.

key: you may hand in draft pages to the
name: ch05_essay_printer_steal_force
alt: A student and a printer illustrate steal, force and redo: draft pages sent early and recalled, all pages printed before submitting, and retyping from notes after a jam.
scene: A triptych of three panels in a college computer room, the same student in each: a young woman in her early twenties, hair in a clip, a sling bag and an ID card. A busy shared printer sits on the right of every panel. LEFT panel: she sends draft pages to the printer before deciding to submit; a stack of half-finished pages is in the printer tray, and she is pulling one page back with a recall arrow and an eraser icon, her face uncertain. MIDDLE panel: she stands at the submission box holding a finished, stapled essay, but she waits and points at the printer until the last page has come out; a small clock icon shows submission is slow, and a check mark shows nothing will ever need retyping. RIGHT panel: she has already dropped a cover sheet stamped "submitted" into the box; her draft pages never left her desk, and the printer has jammed with a crumpled page; she calmly sits and retypes the essay from a small notebook of her own notes, with a circular redo arrow over the keyboard. Fluorescent lights, rows of monitors, mild exam-week stress. Labels: "STEAL" above the left panel, "FORCE" above the middle panel, "REDO" above the right panel.

key: Three cooks sharing two burners
name: ch05_three_cooks_two_burners
alt: Three cooks interleave on two burners, and the final dinner tastes as if they had cooked one after another in some order.
scene: A wide view of a small Indian home kitchen with a single two-burner gas stove on a granite counter, steel utensils on a rack and a window with a potted chilli plant. Three cooks share the stove in a lively, overlapping way: a grandmother in a cotton saree stirring dal in a pressure cooker on the left burner, a young man in a T-shirt and apron flipping rotis on a tawa that he has just slid onto the right burner, and a teenage girl in a school uniform waiting with a small pan of tea, timing her turn. Thin coloured ribbons trace when each cook used each burner, crossing and interleaving above the stove. On the dining table in the foreground, three finished dishes are laid out, and a small floating thought bubble above the table shows the same three cooks standing in a tidy queue, one after another, holding the same three dishes, with an equals sign between the busy kitchen and the tidy queue. The order in the queue bubble is not the order they started in, to show any order is fine. Warm afternoon light, steam, cheerful family mood. Label: "SERIALIZABLE" above the queue bubble.

key: A wiki page with edit history
name: ch05_wiki_revisions_snapshot
alt: Readers who opened a page at 10:00 keep seeing that saved revision while an editor types an unsaved draft.
scene: A wide view of a shared office with three desks, each with a monitor showing the same generic encyclopedia-style web page with a small revision label in its corner. LEFT: a reader, a middle-aged man in a sweater, looks at his screen showing the page with "rev 10:00", with a small clock on his desk that also shows 10:00 to mark when he opened it. CENTRE: a second reader, a young woman with headphones, opened the page later; her screen shows "rev 10:30", the newest saved version before her time. RIGHT: an editor in her thirties types rapidly on a keyboard; her screen shows the page with a shaded draft overlay and a blinking cursor, and a translucent bubble from her draft floats up but is blocked from reaching the other screens by a thin dotted wall, as nobody else can see it yet. Above the scene, a horizontal strip shows a stack of saved revisions like cards in a timeline marked 9:00, 10:00, 10:30, with arrows from each reader to the card they see. Soft office lighting, calm concentration. Labels: "SNAPSHOT" above the readers, "UNCOMMITTED" above the editor's draft.

key: The latch is the editor software making
name: ch05_lock_vs_latch_document
alt: A long lock held by a person editing a paragraph for minutes, and a tiny latch inside the computer guarding bytes for microseconds.
scene: A split composition in an office meeting room. The LARGE upper part shows a laptop on a conference table with a shared document open; a woman in her thirties, Asha, in a formal kurta, sits typing in paragraph 3, which is highlighted with a coloured border and a small name flag above it. Two colleagues sit across the table, one waiting with arms folded and glancing at the wall clock that shows minutes passing, another reading a different paragraph freely. Below, separated by a thin line, a SMALL magnified cutaway zooms inside the laptop like looking through a microscope: two tiny glowing keystroke characters race toward the same memory cell on a chip, and a tiny turnstile gate lets only one through at a time, with a stopwatch beside it showing a microsecond tick. A dotted zoom cone connects the highlighted paragraph down to the magnified chip. Natural daylight in the room, cool blue light inside the chip, calm and explanatory mood. Labels: "LOCK" beside the name flag on paragraph 3, "LATCH" beside the tiny turnstile.

key: The building directory in the lobby
name: ch05_moved_staff_door_sign
alt: Half an office moves next door; a sign on the old door redirects a visitor who used the outdated lobby directory one door to the right.
scene: A cutaway view of an office corridor with two adjacent rooms, and a lobby at the far left. LEFT: in the lobby, a printed directory board on the wall still lists everyone in the old room, and a worker on a ladder is only just starting to update it with a fresh sheet. CENTRE: the old room, now half empty, with desks for the remaining staff; on its door hangs a hand-written sign with an arrow pointing right that reads "names after Kumar: next room". RIGHT: the new room next door, where staff are unpacking boxes, one man placing a nameplate on his new desk. In the corridor, a visitor in his thirties with a laptop bag and visitor badge, who has just read the old lobby directory, stands at the old door reading the sign, and a curved green arrow carries him one door to the right, where the person he wants, a woman in a blue blouse, waves at him. Bright corridor lighting, moving boxes stacked against the wall, practical, reassuring mood. Labels: "HIGH KEY" on the door sign, "SIBLING LINK" along the curved arrow.

key: Every variant keeps the same drawers
name: ch06_three_catalogue_clerks
alt: Three clerks at the same alphabetical card catalogue: one writes a fresh card, one collects corrections in a tray, one appends sticky notes tracked on a lookup sheet.
scene: A wide view of a library catalogue room with one long row of identical wooden card-catalogue drawers, alphabetical labels on each, shared across three working zones. LEFT: a young clerk in a crisp shirt writes a brand-new index card at a small desk instead of erasing an old one; the old card is lifted out between two fingers and the new one is slid into exactly the same place, with a small swap arrow. CENTRE: an older clerk in a sweater vest drops correction slips into a wire tray on her desk throughout the day, the tray filling up; a wall clock shows evening, and a small inset shows her filing the whole tray into the drawers at once. RIGHT: a third clerk, a woman with her hair in a bun and a pencil in it, never opens the drawers; she sticks small yellow sticky notes on the drawer fronts, stacked on top of each other, and keeps a clipboard lookup sheet listing each drawer and the number of its newest sticky note, with a dotted arrow from the sheet to the top note. The drawers themselves look identical in all three zones. Warm wooden tones, filtered daylight, gentle, comparative mood. Labels: "COPY-ON-WRITE" above the left zone, "LAZY" above the centre zone, "BW-TREE" above the right zone.

key: Hand the paper to a clerk who fills
name: ch06_form_three_ways_to_edit
alt: Three ways to change a paper form: write on it directly, retype it into a spreadsheet and reprint, or dictate to a clerk who writes on it for you.
scene: A triptych of three panels at a government office counter, the same applicant in each: a man in his forties with a moustache, a short-sleeved shirt and a folder of documents, filling the same printed application form. LEFT panel: he writes directly on the paper form with a blue ballpoint pen, the form lying flat on the counter. MIDDLE panel: he sits at a computer and types the form's fields into a spreadsheet on screen, edits a cell with ease, and a printer beside him slides out a freshly printed copy of the form; the original paper form still lies on the counter beside it, with a small two-copies icon over both. RIGHT panel: he stands with hands behind his back, dictating, while a clerk in a khaki uniform with spectacles fills in the boxes on the paper for him with a fountain pen; a speech bubble from the applicant connects by an arrow straight to the box the clerk is writing in, and the applicant's hands never touch the paper. Background of steel cupboards, files tied with red tape and a ceiling fan, neutral daylight. Labels: "IN PLACE" above the left panel, "COPY" above the middle panel, "WRAPPER" above the right panel.

key: An inbox tray on your desk (head tree)
name: ch06_inbox_tray_to_archive
alt: Papers are rearranged freely in an inbox tray, sorted into a filing box when full, and filing boxes are merged into a big archive box below without opening it for single sheets.
scene: A vertical cross-section of an office desk and the floor below it, read from top to bottom. TOP: on the desk, a small wire inbox tray where a young office worker in a light kurta and spectacles freely drops and rearranges loose papers with her hands, a few sheets fluttering. MIDDLE: under the desk, a medium cardboard filing box; she has just sorted a full stack from the tray and is dropping it in as one neat bundle, a single downward arrow showing the whole tray moving in one go. BOTTOM: on the floor below, a large heavy archive box with a lid; a fat bundle from the filing box is being merged into it in one big operation, a second downward arrow, and the archive box carries a sticky note with a crossed-out single sheet, showing nobody ever opens it to insert just one paper. Each level is larger than the one above it, like a pyramid of boxes. A wall calendar, a potted money plant and a steel tumbler of tea sit on the desk. Soft office daylight, calm, systematic mood. Labels: "HEAD TREE" beside the inbox tray, "MERGE" beside the lower arrow.

key: A cache-aware packer packs perfectly
name: ch06_packing_for_any_bag
alt: A traveller packs items that are used together next to each other, so whatever bag size she is handed, related things travel together.
scene: A wide view of a bedroom floor during packing for a trip. In the CENTRE, a woman in her thirties in a casual T-shirt and track pants arranges her things in small nested groups: a toothbrush with toothpaste in one pouch, that pouch next to a towel; a charger with a phone stand; socks rolled inside shoes; each group sitting together, like dolls nested inside each other. Around her, three containers of very different sizes are offered by family members: a shoebox held by a child, a carry-on bag held by her husband, and a big metal trunk pushed by her mother. Thin dotted outlines show that whichever container she uses, the nested groups slide in without being split apart. In a small inset on the right, a different traveller has packed perfectly for the carry-on only, every corner filled; when handed the shoebox, his groups are cut in half, with a red cross. Train tickets and a water bottle lie on the bed. Afternoon window light, cheerful and clever mood. Labels: "CACHE-OBLIVIOUS" above the centre group, "CACHE-AWARE" above the inset.

key: A strike-through in the ledger
name: ch07_tombstone_cancel_line
alt: Instead of removing an old ledger line written in ink, a new line saying item 7 cancelled is added, and the person totalling skips item 7.
scene: A close top-down view of an old bound ledger lying open on a shop counter in a wholesale cloth market, entries written in dark blue ink. Line by line, items are listed, and line 7 shows a bolt of cotton with a price. The old line cannot be removed: an eraser lies nearby with a red cross over it, and a small inset shows the same line 7 copied into two other notebooks on a shelf, also in ink. At the bottom of the page, the trader, an elderly man in a white kurta with a pencil behind his ear and round spectacles, writes a new line with a steady hand: "item 7: cancelled". On the right edge of the page, a younger accountant, his nephew in a checked shirt, runs a pencil down the column while adding a total on a calculator; when his pencil reaches line 7, a curved arrow loops down to the cancellation line at the bottom and back, and he skips item 7 with a small hop mark. Warm lamp light, bales of fabric in the background, careful, traditional mood. Label: "TOMBSTONE" next to the cancellation line.

key: including the copy in the archive
name: ch07_tombstone_archive_copy
alt: A cancelled sticky note may only be thrown away once the archive copy downstairs is gone; thrown away early, the old archive order looks valid again.
scene: A two-level cutaway of a small office. UPSTAIRS: a desk with an order slip that has a bright red sticky note on it reading "cancelled"; a young clerk in a sweater is reaching to peel the sticky note off and drop it in a bin. DOWNSTAIRS: a dim archive room with steel shelves of box files, where an older copy of the same order slip still sits inside one box, with no note on it. In the main view, a thin dotted line connects the upstairs order to its downstairs copy. A small two-step strip at the side tells the outcome: in step one, the clerk throws the sticky note away too early; in step two, a colleague with spectacles pulls the archive copy, sees no cancellation anywhere and happily stamps it "valid", while a ghostly red exclamation mark hovers over it. A second tiny inset shows the right order of events: the archive copy is shredded first, then the sticky note goes in the bin, with a green check mark. Warm light upstairs, cool dim light downstairs, cautionary mood. Label: "TOMBSTONE" on the red sticky note, "RESURRECTED" over the archive copy in the side strip.

key: Each cook knows only what is on
name: ch08_kitchen_cooks_shouting
alt: A restaurant kitchen where cooks know only their own station and shout across the room to coordinate, cooperate, pass news and agree on a special.
scene: A wide overhead view of a large Indian restaurant kitchen with four separate cooking stations arranged around the room, steam and clatter everywhere. At the TOP, the head chef, a broad man in his fifties with a tall white hat, hands order slips to cooks, with arrows going out to each station. On the LEFT, two cooks, a young man at the tandoor and a woman at the curry station, wait for each other with plates in hand, a dotted line between their plates showing that the dish can only go out when both parts are ready. On the RIGHT, a chain of three speech bubbles passes from cook to cook across the room, each bubble showing a tiny basil leaf with a cross, as the news that basil has run out travels. At the BOTTOM, all four cooks raise thumbs toward a small chalkboard reading "tonight: biryani", agreeing on one special. Each cook's station has a little thought bubble with only their own pans in it. A noisy exhaust fan and clanging pots partly drown out one shout, drawn as a broken speech bubble. Warm, steamy light, energetic mood. Labels: "COORDINATION" by the head chef, "CONSENSUS" by the chalkboard.

key: You post a cheque and hear nothing
name: ch08_posted_cheque_silence
alt: A man waits at his kitchen table for news of a posted cheque; it could be lost, stuck at the bank, cashed without a receipt or the bank closed, and all look the same.
scene: A central scene of a quiet kitchen table in an Indian flat, where a retired man in his sixties, white vest and spectacles, sits with his chin in his hand staring at an empty letterbox slot in the door and a wall calendar with two weeks crossed off. Around him, arranged in a ring of five thought-bubble vignettes connected to his head by small dotted lines, are the possibilities: an envelope lying lost in a muddy gutter under rain; the same envelope sitting in a tall unsorted pile at a bank counter; a bank clerk stamping the cheque as cashed while the receipt slip blows away out of a window; a bank building with its shutters down and a closed sign; and a postman's bag with the letter still inside, stuck at a sorting centre. All five vignettes lead back to the same thing in the centre: a blank speech bubble over the empty letterbox, showing silence. A cup of tea has gone cold on the table. Soft afternoon light, patient, slightly anxious mood. Label: "SILENCE" inside the blank bubble over the letterbox.

key: A cross-country call is posting a letter
name: ch08_next_desk_vs_letter
alt: Asking the colleague at the next desk is instant; posting a letter across the country always takes time, and a parcel longer than a postcard.
scene: A split-panel scene divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a small open-plan office; a young man in a formal shirt leans over a low partition to ask the colleague at the next desk, a woman in her twenties with headphones around her neck, a quick question; her reply bubble appears instantly, and a tiny stopwatch on the partition shows almost zero time. RIGHT panel: a map of India stretches across the panel, with the same young man on the far left at a red post box dropping in two items, a thin postcard and a fat parcel. Dotted travel paths run across the map toward a distant city, passing through a train, a sorting office and a mail van. The postcard's path is shorter with a small calendar showing two days; the parcel's path has a heavier truck icon and a calendar showing five days. Both arrive safely with check marks, showing nothing was lost but nothing was instant. Bright daytime light, clear, informative mood. Labels: "LOCAL CALL" above the left panel, "REMOTE CALL" above the right panel.

key: Comparing the watch faces cannot tell
name: ch08_two_watches_who_is_late
alt: Two friends meet at 6 with watches set by eye, one five minutes slow, each sure the other is late; only a message between them settles who came first.
scene: A wide scene outside a busy Indian railway station clock tower at dusk, where two friends in their twenties meet. On the LEFT, a young man in a hoodie with a backpack holds up his wrist watch showing six o'clock exactly, pointing at it accusingly. On the RIGHT, a young woman in a kurta and jeans with a tote bag holds up her own watch, which shows five minutes to six, and points back at him with an equally accusing face. Above them, two thought bubbles each contain a little picture of the other friend arriving late. Between them on the ground, the two watch faces are drawn large side by side, clearly showing different times, with a big question mark between them. In the background, a dotted line shows a text message travelling from her phone to his phone, with a small timestamp envelope icon that he will receive, suggesting that only something passed between them can order events. The station clock tower behind them is in shadow so it cannot settle the dispute. Autos, a chai stall and evening crowds around them, warm orange sky, playful mood. Label: "CLOCK DRIFT" between the two watch faces.

key: Two post offices with different street
name: ch08_two_maps_post_offices
alt: Two post offices hold different maps; one delivers a parcel to a new building, the other searches the old address and reports it never arrived.
scene: A split-panel scene divided by a thin vertical line, each showing a small Indian post office back room with a big street map pinned on the wall. LEFT panel: the map is new and shows a tall new apartment building drawn in a cleared plot; a postman in khaki rides off on a bicycle, and a dotted delivery path ends at that new building, where a woman receives the parcel at the gate with a smile and a check mark. RIGHT panel: the map is old and yellowed, and the same plot is still shown as an empty field; a second postman stands at the empty field with the parcel under his arm, scratching his head, then a small inset shows him back at the counter telling a customer "not delivered" with an apologetic shrug. The two maps are clearly different side by side, one with the building, one without. Both postmen hold identical parcels with the same address. Bright midday light, slightly frustrating, explanatory mood. Labels: "NEW MAP" above the left map, "OLD MAP" above the right map, "STALE STATE" under the right panel.

key: asking a librarian in another city
name: ch08_librarian_over_the_phone
alt: A student reads a book on her desk, versus asking a far-away librarian to read it aloud over the phone while someone edits a later chapter.
scene: A split-panel scene divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a college student in her twenties, braid and a cotton kurta, sits at her own study desk turning pages of a book with ease, a cup of tea beside her and a desk lamp glowing. RIGHT panel: the same student sits at an empty desk holding an old landline phone to her ear, with a long curly cord stretching off across a map to a distant city library, where an elderly librarian with spectacles reads to her down the phone, one word per call, tiny speech bubbles each holding a single word dotted along the cord. In a second inset beneath, the librarian now reads a whole chapter per call with a bigger bubble, but behind the librarian a young man with a pen is crossing out and rewriting a paragraph in chapter 3 while the librarian is still reading chapter 2, with a red question mark linking the two. Warm lamp light on the left, cooler dusk light on the right, thoughtful mood. Labels: "LOCAL" above the left panel, "REMOTE" above the right panel.

key: pushes through the door at once
name: ch08_shop_reopen_rush
