alt: After a power cut a crowd rushes the door at once and nobody gets served; when people return after random delays, the queue moves.
scene: A split-panel scene outside the same small Indian electronics shop, divided by a thin vertical line, a just-restored power indicator light glowing above the door in both. LEFT panel: the shutter has just gone up and a crowd of about twelve people of all ages pushes through the narrow door at the same instant, elbows and bags jammed in the doorway, a frazzled shopkeeper behind the counter unable to serve anyone, with tangled arrows and stress lines. RIGHT panel: the same crowd has dispersed to nearby spots, one person sipping tea at a stall, another sitting on a scooter, another browsing a fruit cart; each has a small clock bubble showing a different random wait of a few minutes, and only two people at a time stroll in through the door, where the smiling shopkeeper hands over a package. A short orderly line forms naturally. Late afternoon sun, busy street with tangled wires overhead, comic but clear mood. Labels: "THUNDERING HERD" above the left panel, "RANDOM BACKOFF" above the right panel.

key: Stubborn is posting the same postcard
name: ch08_postcard_delivery_guarantees
alt: Four ways of sending a postcard: drop it once, ask for a text back, post it every day forever, or post daily until the text arrives.
scene: A grid of four small panels, each showing a young woman in her twenties in a yellow kurta at a red Indian post box, and her friend far away in a small inset circle in the corner. Panel ONE: she drops a single postcard in the box and walks off; a dotted path shows it maybe arriving, maybe falling into a puddle. Panel TWO: she drops a postcard and holds up her phone, waiting for a text bubble reading "got it" from the friend. Panel THREE: a wall calendar shows many days ticked off, and she posts an identical postcard every single day, the friend's mailbox in the inset overflowing with duplicate cards. Panel FOUR: she posts the card daily until her phone shows the "got it" text; then she stops, holding the next card back; in the inset, the friend holds two identical postcards, one extra because the first reply text was lost, shown by a broken text bubble. Bright daylight, playful, diagram-like mood. Labels: "FAIR-LOSS" over panel one, "STUBBORN" over panel three, "RETRANSMIT" over panel four.

key: Pressing a lift button five times
name: ch08_lift_button_vs_pay
alt: Pressing a lift button five times still brings one lift; tapping Pay five times on a slow app can charge five times unless the order number is remembered.
scene: A split-panel scene divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: an apartment building lobby with steel lift doors; a hurried young man in office clothes with a laptop bag jabs the lift call button repeatedly, five little tap marks around his finger, and the floor indicator above shows a single lift coming down; a check mark shows only one lift arrives. RIGHT panel: a close view of a woman's hands holding a phone with a generic shopping app showing a slow spinning loader on a big "Pay" button; five tap marks surround her thumb. Below the phone, two possible outcomes branch: on the bad branch, five identical receipts spill out of a printer with a red cross; on the good branch, a shop clerk at a counter checks a small paper slip with one order number written on it and waves away four duplicate requests with a polite hand, while just one receipt prints with a green check. Clean daytime lighting, light humour. Labels: "IDEMPOTENT" above the left panel, "NOT IDEMPOTENT" above the right panel, "ORDER NUMBER" on the clerk's slip.

key: Chapters of a serialised novel arrive
name: ch08_serial_novel_buffer
alt: Chapters of a novel arrive by post out of order and some twice; a reader stacks early ones on a side table, reads in order, bins repeats and keeps a bookmark.
scene: A cosy reading corner in an old Indian house, with a cane armchair, a window and a brass lamp. An elderly woman in her seventies, cotton saree and shawl, round spectacles, sits reading a thin paper booklet marked "ch 4". At her feet the morning post has just come through the door: a scatter of envelopes whose labels read chapter numbers in random order, 6, 5, 7 and another 3. On a small side table to her right sit chapters 6 and 7 stacked and waiting, with a little arrow showing they will be read later. Beside her armchair a small waste basket holds the extra chapter 3, which she has already read, with a tiny cross. A cloth bookmark with a tassel rests on a small shelf next to a card with the number 4, marking the last chapter she has finished. A ginger cat sleeps on a cushion nearby, a postman's cycle is visible through the window, and a cup of tea steams on the windowsill. Warm morning light, peaceful, orderly mood. Labels: "BUFFER" above the side table, "DUPLICATE" above the waste basket, "NPROCESSED" by the bookmark.

key: If the same invoice comes back, they see
name: ch08_paid_stamp_dedup
alt: A cashier sees the PAID stamp on a returned invoice and hands back the receipt instead of charging again.
scene: A medium shot of a cashier's counter at a busy Indian wholesale shop, with ledgers, a cash box and a rubber-stamp rack. The cashier, a woman in her forties in a printed saree with reading glasses on a beaded chain, has just been handed an invoice for the second time by a delivery boy in a cap. On the counter in front of her, the invoice clearly shows a big red rubber-stamp mark reading "PAID" across it. Her right hand is already holding out a small receipt slip to the boy, not opening the cash box, which stays shut with a little lock icon. In a small inset bubble at the top, the earlier moment: the same invoice arriving the first time, the cashier entering the payment in a ledger and thumping the red stamp onto it. Behind the boy, a second identical copy of the invoice flutters in from a courier bag, with a small number 2 tag on it, showing it was delivered twice. Bright shop lighting, sacks of grain stacked in the back, a calendar and a ceiling fan overhead, calm, efficient mood. Label: "EXACTLY ONCE" above the cashier.

key: Agreeing by text to meet tonight
name: ch08_two_generals_texting
alt: Two friends keep texting confirmations about meeting at 8, and whoever sent the last text can never be sure it arrived.
scene: A split composition with two young friends in different homes, connected across the middle by a long zigzag of text bubbles. On the LEFT, a young man in his twenties sits on his bed in a hostel room, phone in hand; on the RIGHT, a young woman sits at a balcony in her flat, also on her phone. Between them, a ladder of chat bubbles alternates sides from top to bottom: "8?" from him, "Yes!" from her, "Confirmed?" from him, "Confirmed!" from her, "Got it?" from him, each smaller than the one before, trailing off into dots. The very last bubble, in the middle of the gap, is drawn half-faded with a broken dotted path and a small question mark over it, not clearly reaching the other phone. Both friends look uncertain, the man biting his lip, the woman typing yet another reply. A wall clock in each room shows the evening approaching 8, and a half-packed bag and a mirror in each room hint that both are already getting ready to go out, just in case. Soft evening light, gentle comic tension. Label: "TWO GENERALS" across the top of the chat ladder.

key: Three friends choosing a restaurant
name: ch08_three_friends_silent_vote
alt: Two friends have voted opposite ways for a restaurant and wait on the silent third friend, with no clock to say time is up.
scene: A three-part scene connected by a group-chat strip running across the top. On the LEFT, a young woman in a café holds up her phone showing her vote, a small dosa icon; in the CENTRE, a young man on a bus holds up his phone showing his vote, a small pizza icon; on the RIGHT, the third friend, a young man in a dim room, is shown only as a silhouette with his phone face down on a table, a single typing-dots bubble hovering ambiguously over it that may or may not turn into a message. The chat strip at the top shows one vote for each restaurant and an empty grey slot for the third. The two voters look at each other's phones with puzzled faces: one has a thought bubble of going ahead without him and him suddenly sending a vote that flips the result, and the other has a thought bubble of waiting forever, with a spider web growing over a calendar. Importantly, there is no clock anywhere in the scene, and a crossed-out hourglass icon floats above the chat strip. Muted evening light, unresolved mood. Label: "FLP" above the empty grey slot.

key: Crash-stop is a committee member who
name: ch08_committee_crash_stop_recovery
alt: One committee member leaves the meeting and does not return; another steps out and comes back, and without notes might vote twice.
scene: A split-panel scene of the same housing-society committee meeting in a small community hall, divided by a thin vertical line, with members sitting around a table with a ballot box. LEFT panel: an elderly member in a white kurta and Nehru cap stands up and walks out through the door with his umbrella; the door closes behind him, and his empty chair has a small sign reading "until next meeting"; the others continue without him. RIGHT panel: a middle-aged member in a checked shirt steps out to take a phone call, a dotted path loops out of the door and back in; he returns to his chair looking confused, his memory bubble empty. He is about to drop a second ballot into the box, while the ballot box already holds his first vote, marked with a small matching number tag. A small inset beside him shows the safe alternative: a notepad in his pocket reading "voted: yes", which he checks before voting again, with a green check mark. Tube lights, a framed photo on the wall, plastic chairs, light comic mood. Labels: "CRASH-STOP" above the left panel, "CRASH-RECOVERY" above the right panel.

key: Byzantine: one who replies promptly
name: ch08_omission_vs_byzantine_colleague
alt: One colleague sometimes never replies or replies late; another replies at once with confident but wrong and different answers to different people.
scene: A split-panel scene in an open office, divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a relaxed colleague in his forties, sweater and loose tie, leans back in his chair asleep, a pile of unopened envelopes and a monitor full of unread email icons in front of him; a calendar shows one reply finally being sent a week late, a snail icon carrying it to a waiting coworker. RIGHT panel: a sharply dressed colleague in her thirties with a confident smile sits at a desk, rapidly firing replies; three coworkers stand around her each holding a printed reply, and the three printouts clearly show different answers, one says 42, one says 17, one says 99, each with a little tick of confidence on it, but with red question marks appearing over the coworkers' heads as they compare notes. A small two-faced mask icon hovers above her desk, and a water cooler and whiteboard fill the background. Bright office lighting, pot plants, gentle humour with a warning tone. Labels: "OMISSION" above the left panel, "BYZANTINE" above the right panel.

key: A plane with two engines that can fly
name: ch08_plane_masked_engine_failure
alt: A twin-engine plane loses one engine; passengers notice nothing while the cockpit crew switches to a slower checklist.
scene: A cutaway side view of a twin-engine passenger plane cruising above white clouds. The left engine is shown with a thin wisp of smoke and its fan stopped, a small red warning symbol beside it; the right engine glows and turns normally. In the passenger cabin, rows of passengers carry on as usual: a family sharing snacks, a student asleep with headphones, a businessman reading a newspaper, a flight attendant smiling as she pours tea, none of them noticing anything. In the cockpit at the front, two pilots, a woman captain in her forties and a younger male first officer, calmly work through a thick laminated checklist marked "engine out" with a pen, an amber light on the panel. A dotted speed gauge on the cockpit wall shows the needle moved a little lower than before. Outside the windows the sky is bright blue and calm, and the plane stays perfectly level on its route line. Calm, reassuring mood with a hint of tension only in the cockpit. Labels: "MASKED" above the cabin, "SLOW PATH" above the cockpit checklist.

key: A teacher calling the register
name: ch09_register_late_here
alt: A teacher calling the register moves to the next name while a pupil's late reply is still on its way, so the pupil is marked absent.
scene: A wide view of an Indian government school classroom with wooden benches, a blackboard and a ceiling fan. At the front, a teacher in her forties in a cotton saree holds an attendance register and a pen, calling out names; her speech bubble already shows the next roll number, 15, and her pen is putting an "A" next to number 14 in the register. In the back row, a small boy in a white shirt and blue shorts, roll number 14 pinned on his pocket, has just looked up from a daydream and raised his hand, and his speech bubble "here!" is shown drifting slowly forward over the heads of the other pupils, still in mid-air halfway across the room. A dotted line from his bubble ends in a small cross before reaching the teacher, as it will land after she has moved on and be credited to nothing. Other pupils turn to look at him, some giggling. A window shows a sunny schoolyard with a mango tree. Bright morning light, gently comic mood. Labels: "TIMEOUT" above the register, "LATE REPLY" beside the floating bubble.

key: A chain letter that everyone signs
name: ch09_chain_letter_tallies
alt: Letters passed hand to hand collect signatures; a tally board shows one person's count still rising and another's frozen.
scene: A wide scene of a community hall where many people of different ages sit in a loose circle, passing paper letters from hand to hand in all directions, each person adding a small signature before passing it on. In the foreground, a young man in a kurta and spectacles sits at a small desk with a chalk tally board beside him; he never writes to anyone, he just looks at each letter that passes him and adds tally marks next to the names of the signatures he sees. On the tally board, the name of a lively grandmother, shown across the hall signing busily, has a long and still-growing row of tally marks with an upward arrow. Another name, belonging to a man shown asleep in a chair in the far corner with his pen fallen to the floor, has a short row of tally marks with no new ones, and a small frozen snowflake icon beside it. Above the board, a ruler-like bracket with a question mark asks how far behind a tally must fall before giving up. Warm afternoon light through tall windows, friendly, buzzing mood. Labels: "HEARTBEAT COUNTER" above the tally board, "FROZEN" beside the stalled row.

key: about 20 minutes after leaving
name: ch09_home_safe_unease_meter
alt: Waiting for a home-safe text, worry rises from calm at 22 minutes to near certainty at 35, faster for a punctual friend than for an unpredictable one.
scene: A sequence of three panels showing the same young woman in her twenties at home in pyjamas and a T-shirt, sitting on a sofa with her phone, waiting for a friend's message after the friend left her house. In each panel, a wall clock shows minutes since the friend left, and a vertical thermometer-style worry meter is mounted on the wall beside her. Panel ONE: clock at 22 minutes, meter low and green, she scrolls her phone relaxed. Panel TWO: clock at 26 minutes, meter in the middle and yellow, she sits up, frowning at the phone. Panel THREE: clock at 35 minutes, meter high and red near a marked line at the top, and she is lifting the phone to her ear to call. A small inset bubble under the panels compares two friends: one with a tidy, narrow timing curve, a punctual friend who always arrives at about 20, and one with a wide flat curve, a friend who arrives anywhere between 10 and 60, with the worry meter for the second barely moving at 35. Warm night-time lamp light, gently tense mood. Labels: "PHI" beside the worry meter, "THRESHOLD" at the marked line.

key: A queue at a passport office where
name: ch10_passport_queue_flapping
alt: At a passport office the highest ticket number is always served first, so a man who keeps leaving and returning keeps interrupting the clerk.
scene: A wide view of a passport office waiting hall with rows of plastic chairs, a token display board and a single service counter. Behind the counter, a clerk in his thirties in a formal shirt and lanyard has been interrupted mid-task, papers half-stamped, as a man in a hurry, middle-aged with a sweaty brow and car keys in hand, rushes back to the counter waving a token with the highest number on it, the display board flashing his number. Behind him, a dotted path loops out of the glass door to a parking meter on the street and back in again, drawn three times, showing he keeps leaving and returning. Each time he comes back, a red interruption spark appears over the clerk's desk. In the queue, other applicants wait patiently, including an old woman with a file and a student with a backpack. A small inset at the top right shows a better rule: a clipboard ranking applicants by a reliability star rating alongside the number, and the restless man has only one star. Fluorescent lighting, slightly chaotic mood. Labels: "HIGHEST ID" on the display board, "FLAPPING" along the looping dotted path.

key: Nobody has to hold a team-wide vote
name: ch10_whiteboard_successor_list
alt: A team lead on leave leaves a successor list on the whiteboard; a teammate calls the first name, who takes charge and posts to the team channel.
scene: A three-step scene in a small team office with a whiteboard, laptops and a potted plant. Step ONE, on the LEFT: the team lead, a man in his forties with a beard and a backpack and a travel pillow round his neck, writes on the whiteboard before leaving: "1. Priya" and "2. Ravi", with a small arrow from the first name to the second. Step TWO, in the CENTRE: the next morning, a young engineer in a hoodie notices the lead's empty chair and calls the first name on the whiteboard from her phone; no group of people is gathered, and there is no ballot box, which appears crossed out in a small icon. Step THREE, on the RIGHT: Priya, a woman in her thirties in a smart blouse, answers on a video call with a confident thumbs up, then posts a short message in the team channel on her laptop, shown as a big chat bubble reading "I've got it" with several emoji reactions from teammates. Ravi, in the background, relaxes back in his chair, not needed. Bright office daylight, smooth, efficient mood. Labels: "SUCCESSORS" above the whiteboard list, "NEW LEADER" above Priya.

key: it is cheaper to move the 3 into the big
name: ch10_merge_group_chats
alt: Two group chats planning the same event merge by moving the 3 people of the small group into the 40-person group and telling only those 3 about the new admin.
scene: A wide illustration of two large smartphone screens floating side by side, each showing a generic group chat with a list of round profile icons. The LEFT phone shows a big group with about forty small avatars and an admin badge on one of them, a woman in a red saree. The RIGHT phone shows a tiny group with only three avatars and its own admin, a young man in a cap. Between the phones, the two admins are shown as small figures shaking hands on a bridge drawn between the screens. Three small avatars are lifting out of the small group and travelling along a curved arrow into the big group. A single welcome message bubble, addressed only to the three newcomers, reads "your new admin is Meera", while the forty members in the big group carry on chatting undisturbed with no new notifications. A crossed-out inset shows the costly alternative: forty notification bells ringing at once. Clean bright background with festive bunting hinting at the event being planned, cheerful, clever mood. Labels: "SMALL INTO BIG" above the arrow, "MERGE" above the handshake.

key: Head office phones every branch when
name: ch11_price_list_three_branches
alt: Head office updates a price and phones three branches; branch C has not picked up yet, so a shopper there still sees the old price.
scene: A wide illustrated map-like scene with a head office building at the top and three branch shops below it, connected by telephone wires. At HEAD OFFICE, a manager in her forties in a blazer writes a new price on a big price board, crossing out 120 and writing 135, while a speech bubble from a clerk tells a waiting customer "price updated". The phone wires carry little ringing symbols down to each branch. At BRANCH A, the shopkeeper is on the phone and already changing the shelf tag to 135. At BRANCH B, a young assistant hangs up and writes 135. At BRANCH C, on the right, the phone on the counter is ringing with shaking lines but nobody has picked it up; the shopkeeper is busy weighing rice for a customer, and a shopper in a kurta holding a packet looks at a shelf tag still showing the old price 120. The packet is the same item in all three shops. Nobody looks upset; a small floating rulebook icon with a question mark hovers between the branches, asking which answers are allowed. Bright daytime light, neutral, explanatory mood. Label: "CONSISTENCY MODEL" on the floating rulebook.

key: A spare tyre makes the car
name: ch11_spare_tyre_replica
alt: After a puncture, an inflated spare tyre saves the trip, while a flat spare is useless; replicas only help if kept up to date.
scene: A split-panel roadside scene on an Indian highway, divided by a thin vertical line, a hatchback car with a punctured front tyre in both. LEFT panel: a father in his forties in a half-sleeve shirt pulls the spare tyre from the boot; it is plump and firm, he gives a thumbs up, and his family waits happily by the road eating roasted corn from a vendor, a small green check above the car. RIGHT panel: the same father pulls out a spare that is completely flat and sagging, cobwebs on it, and he stares at it in dismay while his family sits on the roadside under a tree looking glum, a red cross above the car. In a small inset at the bottom right, a regular habit is shown: a man at a petrol pump air machine checking the spare's pressure with a gauge, a calendar page beside him marking each month, showing the upkeep that makes the spare useful. Bright afternoon sun, a dhaba sign and trucks passing in the distance, practical, slightly comic mood. Labels: "REPLICA" on the spare in each panel, "KEEP IT UPDATED" above the inset.

key: no shared clock that settles which
name: ch11_two_phones_two_orders
alt: Two friends compare phones and see the same two group messages in opposite orders, with no shared clock to settle which came first.
scene: A close medium shot of two friends in their twenties sitting side by side on a college canteen bench, holding their phones up next to each other to compare. The young man on the LEFT wears a denim jacket; the young woman on the RIGHT wears a yellow kurta and has a cup of tea in her other hand. Both phones show the same generic group chat with the same two message bubbles, one blue bubble with a small cricket bat icon and one green bubble with a small umbrella icon. On the man's phone, the blue bubble is on top; on the woman's phone, the green bubble is on top. Thin arrows from each bubble down to tiny timestamps show different local receipt times on each phone. Both friends look at each other with amused confusion, each pointing at their own screen as if it were right. Above them, a large wall clock is drawn with its face blank and a question mark in the centre, showing there is no shared clock that can settle it. Canteen background with steel tables, a samosa counter and a menu board, bright midday light, light-hearted mood. Label: "WHICH WAS FIRST" above the blank clock.

key: Stronger models are stricter rulebooks
name: ch11_league_rulebook_referees
alt: A rulebook narrows the wild possibilities of a game so referees can judge it; a stricter rulebook is easier to referee but slower to play.
scene: A wide view of a local football ground with two halves of the field, separated by a thin chalk line, a referee in black with a whistle in each half. LEFT half: a chaotic picture of everything that could happen without rules, players picking up the ball and running off the pitch, one climbing the goalpost, one sitting on the ball, with the referee helpless and confused, scratching his head. RIGHT half: a thick rulebook stands upright on a small table at the touchline, and the game is orderly: players stay inside the lines, a foul is clearly marked, and the referee confidently blows the whistle and points. A small inset at the bottom right shows a third, even stricter version, with a thicker rulebook and players moving slowly in single file, the referee relaxed with a stopwatch showing the game running long. Spectators in the stands, a chai vendor, and floodlight poles add atmosphere. Late afternoon golden light, playful mood. Labels: "NO MODEL" above the left half, "MODEL" above the rulebook, "STRONGER" above the inset.

key: A light switch in Mumbai and a bulb
name: ch11_switch_and_far_bulb
alt: A switch in Mumbai and a bulb in New York connected by a long wire; the bulb cannot glow before the signal arrives.
scene: A wide, map-like illustration of a curved globe segment showing India on the LEFT and the east coast of North America on the RIGHT, with an ocean between them. In Mumbai, a woman in her thirties in a cotton saree stands in her flat, her finger pressing down a white wall switch. In New York, a light bulb hangs from a ceiling in a small apartment, where a man in a sweater looks up at it expectantly. A long glowing wire arcs over the globe between the two, and a small pulse of light is shown travelling along the wire, only partway across the ocean, with a tiny stopwatch beside it showing time passing. The bulb in New York is still dark. A faded ghostly version of the bulb shown already glowing, with a red cross over it, represents what strict consistency would require: glowing before the pulse could arrive. Night sky with stars above the globe, a crescent moon, a sense of vast distance, thoughtful mood. Labels: "STRICT CONSISTENCY" above the crossed-out glowing bulb, "SIGNAL TRAVEL TIME" along the wire.

key: A train ticket gate. You may push
name: ch11_turnstile_and_aba_cup
alt: A metro turnstile turns exactly once while the light is green; separately, a coffee cup is swapped for an identical one while its owner is away.
scene: A split-panel scene divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a metro station ticket gate with a green light glowing on top; a commuter in his twenties with a backpack pushes through the turnstile arm. A thin timeline beneath the gate shows a green band between two marks, and a single bright dot inside that band marks the one instant the arm turned. He is shown fully outside in a ghosted image before the dot and fully inside after it, never halfway. RIGHT panel: a three-step strip at an office desk. Step one: a woman in a cardigan sets down a white paper coffee cup and walks away to a meeting. Step two: a colleague in a hoodie picks it up and drinks it, then places a new identical cup in the exact same spot. Step three: the woman returns, checks the cup's colour, size and position with a magnifying glass, and is satisfied, while a small thought bubble above the desk shows the hidden swap she cannot detect. Bright station lighting on the left, warm office light on the right. Labels: "LINEARIZATION POINT" under the timeline dot, "ABA" above the right panel.

key: A news ticker shown on many screens
name: ch11_news_ticker_screens
alt: Several screens run the same news ticker late but in the same order; a crossed-out screen showing a different order is what sequential consistency forbids.
scene: A wide view of a railway station concourse with four television screens mounted at different spots, each showing the same scrolling news ticker strip at the bottom. Above the screens, a reporters' desk on the LEFT shows three reporters filing stories, each holding a coloured story card, red, blue and green, with small timestamps showing the order they were filed. Screens one, two and three run the ticker with the stories in the same order, blue then red then green, but each screen is behind by a different amount; small clock badges on the screens show lags of a few seconds, one minute and three minutes. Commuters with suitcases glance up at different screens. Screen four, at the far right, shows the stories in a different order, red then green then blue, and it is crossed out with a bold red cross. A small inset at the top shows a stricter screen in sync with the reporters' clock, labelled with a lightning icon, representing no lag at all. Busy station atmosphere, a tea stall and a departure board, bright daytime light, clear mood. Labels: "SEQUENTIAL" above the three matching screens, "LINEARIZABLE" above the inset.

key: Causal consistency is exactly that rule
name: ch11_causal_group_chat
alt: In a group chat a reply must never appear above the question it answers, while two unrelated messages may appear in either order.
scene: A wide composition with two large smartphones side by side, each held by a different hand, showing the same generic group chat for a group of friends planning a dinner. On BOTH phones, the bubble "Dinner at 8?" appears above the reply "Yes, let's do it!", joined by a small curved arrow from the question to the reply, glowing green to show the order is always kept. Lower down, two unrelated messages, a bubble with a small sun icon reading "Nice weather" and a bubble with a clock icon reading "Running late", appear in opposite orders on the two phones, with a relaxed double-headed arrow between them showing either order is fine. Below the phones, a small crossed-out third phone shows the reply bubble sitting above the question, with a red cross and a confused face emoji. The background is a soft blurred street café scene at evening with fairy lights, a waiter carrying plates of momos past the table. Calm, friendly mood. Labels: "CAUSAL" above the green arrow, "CONCURRENT" above the double-headed arrow.

key: You update your profile photo, refresh
name: ch11_four_session_anomalies
alt: Four phone mishaps: an old profile photo after updating, photos flipping back and forth, a rename reverting, and a reply showing without its comment.
scene: A grid of four small panels, each showing a young person's hands holding a phone with a generic social app, and a small puzzled face in the corner. Panel ONE: a woman uploads a new profile photo of herself in a red dupatta, taps refresh, and the screen still shows her old photo in a blue shirt. Panel TWO: a strip of three refresh screens in a row shows the new photo, then the old photo, then the new photo again, with a looping arrow. Panel THREE: a laptop file icon renamed twice, first to "draft" then to "final", while a colleague's laptop beside it shows the name "draft", with a backward arrow. Panel FOUR: a comment thread where a reply bubble saying "agreed!" appears alone on a friend's phone with an empty dotted outline above it where the original comment should be. Each panel has a small red warning icon, and the same plain blue phone case or blue laptop sticker appears in every panel so they read as one person's ordinary day. Clean, bright background, gently humorous mood. Label: "SESSION GUARANTEES" in one banner across the top of the grid.

key: Gossip in a village. Nobody can tell
name: ch11_village_gossip_settles
alt: News spreads through a village unevenly over days, and by the end of the week everyone tells the same story.
scene: A wide, gently sloping view of a small Indian village with mud-and-brick houses, a well, a banyan tree with a stone platform, fields and a temple, shown in three bands from left to right representing three days. On the LEFT, day one: two women at the well whisper to each other, and a few houses have tiny speech-bubble icons over them while most have none. In the MIDDLE, day three: men chatting on the banyan tree platform, children running between houses, and about half the houses now carry the same speech-bubble icon, though a few show a slightly different version with a question mark. On the RIGHT, day seven: every house shows the identical speech-bubble icon, the village is calm, and an old man on a charpai nods knowingly. Above the scene, a sun moving across the sky and small calendar leaves mark the days passing, with no clock anywhere. Goats graze by the fields and a bullock cart rolls along the lane. Golden light, rustic, peaceful mood. Labels: "EVENTUALLY" over the right band, "NO DEADLINE" beside the calendar leaves.

key: A contract signed in front of five
name: ch11_contract_witnesses_diary
alt: Five witnesses to a contract: three keep photocopies, two note it in diaries, and one diary-keeper holds a copy temporarily for someone who is away.
scene: A wide view of a lawyer's office with wooden furniture, a ceiling fan and shelves of thick files. At the centre table, a contract has just been signed, with a fountain pen resting on it. Around the table stand five witnesses of different ages. Three of them, an older man in a dhoti, a woman in a business suit and a young man in a shirt, each hold a full photocopy of the contract. The other two, a grandmother in a shawl and a college student in a hoodie, each write a single line in a small diary reading "contract signed Tuesday". In a side inset on the right, one copy-holder is shown leaving with a suitcase for a trip, and the student temporarily holds an extra photocopy in a folder with a sticky note reading "until he returns". A bracket drawn around any three of the five shows that every group of three still includes someone holding a copy. Warm afternoon light through wooden blinds, formal but friendly mood. Labels: "FULL REPLICA" above the photocopy holders, "WITNESS" above the diary keepers.

key: Three tally sheets for counting
name: ch11_gate_tally_sheets_crdt
alt: Three gatekeepers count visitors in their own columns; comparing sheets by copying the larger number in each column always gives the same total.
scene: A wide scene at a fair ground with three entrance gates decorated with marigold strings, each staffed by a gatekeeper with a clipboard. Each clipboard holds a tally sheet with three columns, one per gate, and each gatekeeper only writes in their own column, shown with a pen hovering over their own column only: a young man at gate one, a middle-aged woman at gate two, an older man at gate three. In the centre, two of the gatekeepers have met under a tent to compare sheets, and arrows show each copying across the bigger number in each column onto their own sheet, so both sheets end up identical. A small loop of arrows shows the comparing can happen in any order, twice, or late, and still give the same total at the bottom. In a small crossed-out inset on the right, a single shared blackboard reads "count = 41", with three people arguing about who wrote last. A giant wheel, balloon sellers and a candy-floss cart fill the background, bright festive daylight, cheerful mood. Label: "CRDT" above the central tent.

key: Each step down removes one promise
name: ch11_consistency_staircase_ramp
alt: A staircase where each step down drops one ordering promise and gains speed, with a side ramp that skips ordering but makes it not matter.
scene: A side view of a wide stone staircase descending from left to right, with four steps, each step a slightly different colour. At the top step stands a man in formal clothes carrying a heavy backpack labelled with a clock icon, walking slowly. On each lower step, the walker is shown again, each time having dropped one item from his backpack: first a small clock, then a numbered queue ticket, then a little chain link, then finally his pack is almost empty and he is walking briskly. Beside each step, a tiny speedometer shows the needle moving faster and a small open-door icon shows more availability. To the right of the staircase, a smooth curving ramp painted in a different colour runs from the top to the bottom, and a young woman on roller skates glides down it holding a tray of building blocks that fit together in any order, a small puzzle-piece icon beside her. Bright daylight, a clear blue sky and trees in the background, optimistic mood. Labels: "LINEARIZABLE" at the top step, "EVENTUAL" at the bottom step, "CRDT" on the ramp.

key: She tells the odd one out the right
name: ch12_teacher_read_repair
alt: A teacher asks three students for an answer; two say 42, one says 41, and she corrects the odd one out before moving on.
scene: A medium-wide view of a coaching-class room with a whiteboard, wooden desks and a ceiling fan. At the front, a teacher in her thirties in a cotton salwar suit with a marker in hand points at three students in the front row. Each student holds up an open notebook toward her: a boy in a white shirt shows "42", a girl with two plaits shows "42", and a boy with spectacles on the right shows "41". Speech bubbles echo the answers. The teacher has stepped over to the third student and is leaning down, gently writing the correct 42 into his notebook beside the crossed-out 41, while he nods. A small clock above the door shows she is waiting for him to finish correcting before she moves on. In a small inset at the top right, the next teacher, an older man with a moustache, later asks the same boy and gets 42 with a green check. On the whiteboard, only one question is circled, and the rest of the textbook on her desk stays closed, showing she checks only what she asked. Bright morning light, calm, helpful mood. Labels: "READ REPAIR" above the teacher, "BLOCKING" beside the wall clock.

key: Checking whether three copies of a long
name: ch12_contract_checksum_compare
alt: Three holders of a long contract: one reads in full, two send short checksums; one mismatch means fetching that copy and comparing line by line.
scene: A wide scene in a lawyer's chamber with tall shelves of law books and a large wooden table. In the CENTRE, a young lawyer in a black coat and white bands reads one thick copy of a contract in full, a finger moving down the page. To the LEFT and RIGHT, two other copy holders stand at small side tables with their own thick copies closed; instead of handing them over, each sends a small slip of paper toward the centre carrying a short code. The left slip shows "7F3A" and matches a code the lawyer has written on his notepad, with a green check. The right slip shows "9B21", which does not match, with a red cross. In a second small scene at the right edge, the lawyer has fetched that mismatching copy and laid it side by side with his own, comparing line by line with a ruler, a magnifying glass and a pencil, a puzzled expression showing he still cannot tell which copy is newer. Warm afternoon light through tall windows, a ceiling fan, careful, methodical mood. Labels: "DIGEST" above the slips, "FULL COMPARE" above the side-by-side copies.

key: A stamp album with numbered slots
name: ch12_stamp_album_bitmap
alt: A stamp album with numbered slots: a collector describes his gaps compactly and a friend posts exactly the missing stamps 4 and 7.
scene: A close top-down view of a stamp collector's desk with a leather-bound stamp album open on it, tweezers, a magnifying glass and a small lamp. The album page shows a row of eight numbered slots for one friend's stamps: slots 1, 2, 3 hold colourful stamps, slot 4 is empty, slots 5 and 6 hold stamps, slot 7 is empty, and slot 8 holds a stamp. The collector, a retired man in his sixties in a sleeveless sweater with reading glasses, writes on a small postcard: "complete to 3, then 01101". Next to the postcard, a dotted arrow leads to a small inset on the right showing his friend, a cheerful woman of similar age in a shawl, in her own room with a full album, reading the postcard and picking out exactly two stamps, numbered 4 and 7, with tweezers to put in an envelope. A second dotted arrow returns the envelope to the collector. Warm desk lamp light, cosy hobby-room mood with framed stamps on the wall, a cup of tea and a small pot of glue beside the album, and a cat watching from the windowsill. Label: "BITMAP" above the postcard.

key: you phone the full story to two editors
name: ch12_newsroom_eager_lazy
alt: A reporter phones the full story to two editors and sends everyone else a one-line text; someone who got only the text calls back for the story.
scene: A wide view of a busy newsroom with desks, monitors, stacks of newspapers and a wall of clocks. In the CENTRE, a reporter in her thirties with a press badge and a notebook speaks into two phones, one at each ear, connected by thick solid lines to two editors at desks on the LEFT who are writing down the full story. From her laptop, many thin dotted lines go out to desks across the room, each landing on a phone screen with a short text bubble "story #42 out". On the RIGHT, a young sub-editor in a sweater vest holds his phone showing only that short text and looks puzzled; he is now calling back the colleague who texted him, shown as a curved arrow. A small inset at the far right shows the result: from then on, that colleague phones him the full stories directly, with a thick solid line now connecting them. A printing press can be glimpsed through a glass door at the back. Bright fluorescent lighting, energetic, purposeful mood. Labels: "EAGER" over the solid phone lines, "LAZY" over the dotted text lines, "GRAFT" over the new solid line in the inset.

key: Your phone has five favourites you talk
name: ch12_phone_favourites_views
alt: A phone with five favourites and a long contact list; when a favourite stops answering, someone from the long list is promoted, and numbers are swapped at parties.
scene: A wide composition centred on a large smartphone held by a young man in his twenties in a T-shirt. The phone screen shows two sections: at the top, a row of five round favourite contacts with photos; below, a long scrolling list of many rarely called contacts. One favourite circle has gone grey with a small unanswered phone icon, and an arrow shows a contact being lifted from the long list up into the empty favourite spot, with a little star appearing on it. Around the phone, small speech bubbles show him talking daily to the favourites. In the LEFT background, a house party scene with fairy lights and music: he and two friends are holding their phones together, swapping a few numbers, with tiny contact cards flying between phones. The long list on his screen has a few fresh new entries highlighted. Plates of snacks and a speaker sit on a table near the party group. Warm evening light, friendly social mood. Labels: "ACTIVE VIEW" above the favourites row, "PASSIVE VIEW" beside the long list, "SHUFFLE" above the party.

key: Pune subtracts and Delhi adds
name: ch13_two_branches_vanishing_money
alt: A Pune clerk subtracts 300 while the phone line to Delhi dies, so the money vanishes; the safe procedure has both clerks say I can do it before writing in ink.
scene: A split composition with two bank branch counters in different cities, Pune on the LEFT and Delhi on the RIGHT, joined across the middle by a long telephone wire over a faint outline map of India. In the main upper scene, the Pune clerk, a woman in her forties in a printed saree and spectacles, has already written a minus 300 in ink in a thick ledger, while the Delhi clerk, a man in his thirties in a half-sleeve shirt, holds a dead phone receiver with crackling lines and a broken section in the wire between them. A small stack of rupee notes is shown fading into thin air above the middle of the map, with a puff of smoke. In a lower strip, the safe procedure: both clerks speak on the phone and write in pencil, each saying "I can do it" in speech bubbles, then both switch to ink pens together, a green check above each ledger. Background details: bank counters with glass partitions, wall clocks, calendars with a temple picture. Daylight, slightly dramatic upper scene and calm lower strip. Labels: "LOST UPDATE" above the vanishing notes, "BOTH OR NEITHER" above the lower strip.

key: A jury that may only answer
name: ch13_jury_no_liars
alt: A jury can only answer guilty or not, one dissent means no verdict, and a juror who says yes inside and no outside breaks the system.
scene: A split composition in an old courthouse with wooden panelling. The LARGE left part shows a jury room: twelve jurors of different ages and backgrounds sit around a long table, each holding up a small card with either a tick or a cross; eleven show ticks, one older woman in a shawl shows a cross, and the foreman, a man in a brown coat, stands at the head of the table with a large blank verdict sheet, shaking his head, the sheet remaining unsigned. On the wall a framed charge sheet is locked behind glass so nobody can rewrite it. The SMALLER right part, separated by a door, shows a corridor outside: one juror, a man in a grey suit, who had shown a tick inside, is whispering to a reporter with his hand turned down, and a small two-faced mask icon floats over him, with a jagged red crack running from him back across the door into the jury room. Dim afternoon light through tall windows, a jug of water and glasses on the table, serious, cautionary mood. Labels: "UNANIMOUS" above the jury table, "NO LIARS" above the corridor.

key: A group dinner booking needs all five
name: ch13_dinner_booking_timeout
alt: A dinner booking needs all five friends; a silent friend means cancellation before the deadline, and a friend whose phone died must check the chat before assuming it is on.
scene: A two-part scene. The LEFT part shows a restaurant host stand with a reservation book open to a table for five, and a host in a waistcoat holding a phone; a group chat on a large floating phone screen shows four green "I'm in" bubbles and one blank grey slot, and a wall clock passes the deadline, so the host draws a line through the booking. The RIGHT part shows one of the friends, a young man in a hoodie, who had earlier sent "I'm in"; his phone was dead and has just switched back on with a low battery icon. He is standing at his front door in shoes, about to leave, but stops and opens the group chat first, where he sees a message bubble from the host reading "cancelled". A small dotted arrow shows him checking the chat rather than simply heading to the restaurant, with a lightbulb above his head. Evening city lights in the background, auto-rickshaws and street food stalls. Cosy evening light, everyday, slightly comic mood. Labels: "ABORT" above the crossed-out booking, "RECOVERY" above the friend checking the chat.

key: A referee collects sealed votes
name: ch13_referee_collapses_blocking
alt: A referee collects sealed votes and collapses in the corridor, leaving players stuck in the room holding their promises, unable to leave or guess.
scene: A two-room cutaway. On the LEFT, a small meeting room where four players in sports jerseys sit around a table, each with a padlock icon chained to their wrist, looking anxious and bored, a wall clock showing hours passing and cold cups of tea in front of them. A sign on the table reads "promised: yes". On the RIGHT, through an open door, a long corridor where the referee, a man in his fifties in a black-and-white striped shirt, has collapsed on the floor, his whistle beside him. A sealed envelope of votes and a small open notebook lie beside his hand; the notebook page is turned away so the word on it cannot be seen. A faint ghostly speech bubble drifts from his mouth toward a distant open window, as if he might have shouted the result to someone outside. In a small inset at the top, one player who was told the result in an earlier moment shares it with the others, labelled with a green check. Dim corridor light and stuffy room light, tense, waiting mood. Labels: "BLOCKED" above the players, "COORDINATOR DOWN" above the referee.

key: the radio link to two of the four
name: ch13_rocket_split_boosters
alt: A radio arm command reaches only two of four stations; two launch on timeout and two stand down, so the rocket leaves with half its boosters.
scene: A wide launch-pad scene seen from a distance, with a tall rocket in the centre and four boosters strapped around it. At the top LEFT, a mission control room with consoles and a flight director in a headset sends a radio wave; its signal arcs toward four small ground stations arranged in a row beneath the rocket. The arc reaches stations one and two, where operators in white coats hear the word "arm" and start countdown clocks; the arc snaps and breaks halfway to stations three and four, shown with jagged lightning-like breaks and static, and those operators hear nothing and raise their hands in a stand-down gesture. In the main image, the rocket lifts off lopsided: two boosters on the left side fire bright flames, while the two on the right side are dark and falling away. Each station has an open manual on its desk, with a tick, showing everyone followed the rules. Dramatic sky at dawn, smoke clouds, tense, cautionary mood. Labels: "PARTITION" over the broken radio arcs, "HALF COMMIT" above the lopsided rocket.

key: Each shard is a committee (Paxos group)
name: ch13_committees_chairs_wristwatch
alt: Committee chairs negotiate a joint decision, each writing promises into their committee's minutes, while a wristwatch shows a time with a plus-or-minus margin to wait out.
scene: A wide view of a large conference hall divided into three committee tables, each surrounded by five members with name plates. At each table, the chair, marked by a small gavel, leans toward the centre of the hall where the three chairs meet at a small round table to negotiate a joint decision. Behind each chair, a secretary writes every promise the chair makes into a thick minutes book, with a dotted arrow from the chair's speech bubble into the book. At one table, the chair has fainted in his seat and the vice-chair, a woman in a green saree, is already reading the minutes book to carry on. In the foreground, a large close-up of a wristwatch on a chair's wrist shows the time 10:00:00 and a small bracket on the dial with a plus-or-minus margin, and the chair is visibly waiting a moment with a raised finger before stamping a decision. Formal hall with tall curtains and a ceiling fan, steady daylight, organised mood. Labels: "2PC" above the round table of chairs, "PAXOS LOG" on a minutes book, "TRUETIME" beside the wristwatch.

key: Shelving library books by the first
name: ch13_library_shelving_partitioning
alt: Shelving by author letter overloads the S shelf; shelving by scrambled code spreads books but scatters ranges; adding a ninth shelf reshuffles almost every book.
scene: A triptych of three panels in a public library, the same librarian in each: a young man in his twenties in a sweater with a name badge pushing a book trolley. LEFT panel: shelves labelled by letters; the shelf for S is bursting with books piled on top and on the floor, while the shelf for X holds only two lonely books; the librarian is adding two more shelves for S, splitting it into three labelled sections. MIDDLE panel: shelves labelled with scrambled numeric codes, every shelf evenly filled; but a reader holding a list of authors from Sa to Sm walks a long dotted path visiting every single shelf, tired. RIGHT panel: eight numbered shelves and a newly delivered ninth shelf; arrows show almost every book jumping from its old shelf to a new one, books flying in the air, and the librarian looks overwhelmed with his hands on his head. Tall windows, reading tables and green lamps in the background, warm light, gently comic mood. Labels: "RANGE" above the left panel, "HASH" above the middle panel, "MOD N" above the right panel.

key: Committing is peeling the master note
name: ch13_ledger_master_note_percolator
alt: Two ledger lines are pencilled with sticky notes, one master; peeling the master and writing in ink commits, and a later clerk follows a leftover note to finish the job.
scene: A close top-down view of a large shared ledger on a wooden counter, with two lines highlighted: one for Asha and one for Ravi. Both new balances are pencilled lightly in, and each line has a sticky note: Asha's is a bright orange note with a star and the word "master", Ravi's is a yellow note reading "see Asha". The main action: a clerk's hand, with a steel watch and a pen, peels the orange master note off Asha's line and writes "valid from 8" in dark ink in its place, with a small burst of light showing this is the single moment of truth. In a second small strip on the right, the original clerk has fainted in a chair, and a new clerk, a young woman in a cardigan, finds Ravi's leftover yellow note, follows a dotted arrow up to Asha's line, sees the ink, and finishes by inking Ravi's balance and removing his note, with a green check. Soft office light, a calculator, a rubber stamp and a small pad of spare sticky notes beside the ledger, careful mood. Labels: "PRIMARY LOCK" on the orange note, "COMMIT" beside the ink.

key: Two friends update their shared holiday
name: ch13_holiday_plan_ramp_reader
alt: Two friends change a hotel and a flight together; a reader seeing the new hotel notes the paired flight version and asks for it directly instead of waiting.
scene: A wide scene with two large printed itinerary sheets pinned side by side on a corkboard in a living room: one for the hotel, one for the flight. On the LEFT, one friend, a young woman in a T-shirt and shorts, has just pinned a new hotel sheet with a small tag at its corner reading "with flight v2". On the RIGHT, a second friend, a young man in a kurta, is on a ladder, halfway through replacing the flight sheet; the old sheet marked "v1" is still pinned, and he holds the new "v2" sheet in his hand. In the CENTRE foreground, a third friend in glasses holding a cup of coffee reads the hotel sheet, notices the tag, glances at the flight sheet still showing v1, and simply reaches out to take the v2 sheet straight from the second friend's hand, with a curved arrow. Nobody is standing around waiting; a small crossed-out padlock icon floats above the corkboard. Travel brochures and a suitcase on the floor, bright morning light, cheerful mood. Labels: "RAMP" above the corkboard, "NON-BLOCKING" above the reader.

key: Atomic broadcast makes everyone apply
name: ch14_deposit_interest_order
alt: Two bank replicas apply a deposit and 10 percent interest in different orders and end with different balances; atomic broadcast gives one agreed order.
scene: A split composition of two identical bank counters side by side, each with a clerk and a large balance display above it, both starting from the same balance of 1000 shown on a small card at the top. On the LEFT, a clerk in a blue shirt first adds a deposit slip of 100, then applies an interest slip of 10 percent, and his display shows 1210. On the RIGHT, a clerk in a green saree applies the interest slip first and the deposit slip second, and her display shows 1200. The two slips, one a deposit slip with a rupee note icon and one an interest slip with a percent icon, are drawn identically in both panels, just stacked in opposite orders with numbered arrows 1 and 2. Between the counters, a red unequal sign glows. Below both counters, a small strip shows a fix: a single conveyor belt from a central dispatcher delivering the two slips in the same order to both clerks, deposit first, and both displays now read 1210 with green checks. Bank interior with marble floor, a queue barrier and a wall clock, neutral daylight. Labels: "SAME MESSAGES" above the slips, "ATOMIC BROADCAST" above the conveyor belt.

key: A meeting with minutes. A remark counts
name: ch14_minutes_break_view_change
alt: A remark enters the minutes only once everyone has heard it; when someone leaves, the chair closes the section, everyone confirms the same minutes, and a new section begins.
scene: A three-step scene in a wood-panelled meeting room with a long table and a large shared minutes book. Step ONE, on the LEFT: six attendees sit around the table; one speaks, and a remark bubble floats over the table with small ear icons lighting up above each attendee, and only once every ear is lit is the remark written into the minutes book by a secretary. Step TWO, in the CENTRE: one attendee, a man with a briefcase, stands and walks out of the door; the chair, a woman in her fifties in a formal saree, raises her hand to call a break, and the secretary draws a thick double line across the minutes page to close the section. Step THREE, on the RIGHT: each remaining attendee holds up a copy of the minutes and the chair compares them, all identical with green checks, then a fresh section header is written with the new attendee list of five names. A small barrier icon shows nothing from before the double line can be written after it. Warm overhead light, formal but cooperative mood. Labels: "VIEW" above the first section, "VIEW CHANGE" above the double line.

key: Ticket numbers at a deli counter
name: ch14_deli_two_ticket_machines
alt: Two ticket machines at a deli counter print minute dot machine numbers, so every ticket is unique and later minutes win, with the machine number breaking ties.
scene: A medium-wide view of a busy sweet-shop and snacks counter with glass display cases full of samosas and sweets, and a digital board above showing "now serving 5.4". On the LEFT and RIGHT ends of the counter stand two red ticket dispensers, each with a big painted number on its front, 2 on the left machine and 4 on the right machine. Customers pull tickets from both machines: a schoolboy holds a ticket printed "5.2", a woman in a sari holds "5.4", and an old man holds "6.2". A small wall clock above shows minute numbers that match the first part of each ticket. A comparison inset at the top right shows two tickets with the same minute, 5.2 and 5.4, side by side, and a little scale tipping toward 5.4 because its machine number is higher; another shows 6.2 beating both because its minute is later. A shop assistant in a cap and apron behind the counter calls out the numbers. Bright, cheerful shop lighting, bustling and orderly mood. Labels: "MINUTE" on the first part of a big ticket, "MACHINE" on the second part.

key: you drop your form straight into the
name: ch14_classic_vs_fast_clerks
alt: Forms go through one clerk who stamps them in order, or straight into many clerks' inboxes, which saves a trip until two forms collide and a supervisor must sort it out.
scene: A split-panel scene in a government office hall, divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a single clerk in a khaki uniform sits at a desk with a rubber stamp, and a short line of applicants hands him their forms one at a time; he stamps them in order with numbers, and he then passes each stamped form along to a row of other clerks behind him, a slightly longer arrow path. RIGHT panel: two applicants, a young woman with a file and an older man with a cloth bag, drop their forms at the same instant directly into a row of five inbox trays belonging to five clerks; some trays show the woman's form on top and others the man's form on top, with tangled arrows and question marks over the clerks. A stern supervisor in a waistcoat and spectacles walks over and sorts the mismatched trays, with a long clock icon showing this takes more time than the trip saved. Rows of steel cupboards and a ceiling fan in the background, fluorescent light, mild bureaucratic comedy. Labels: "CLASSIC" above the left panel, "FAST" above the right panel, "COLLISION" over the mixed trays.

key: Numbered whiteboards in three rooms
name: ch14_numbered_whiteboards_rooms
alt: Three rooms with numbered write-once whiteboards; before writing board 3 a person crosses out blank lower boards as nil, and a value on board 3 in two rooms is a decision.
scene: A cutaway of three small rooms side by side in an office corridor, each room with an identical row of small numbered whiteboards mounted on the wall, numbered 1, 2, 3 and 4. A woman in her thirties in a blue kurta and lanyard, holding a marker and a small card with the value she wants to write, walks along the corridor with a dotted path visiting two of the rooms. In the first room she visits, she draws a firm cross through blank boards 1 and 2 and writes "nil" on them, and notes that board 2 in the next room already has a value written on it, shown as a small green apple drawing. In her hand, her own card shows a banana, but a small thought bubble shows her switching to the green apple because she saw it already written. In the two visited rooms, board 3 now shows the same green apple, and a bright bracket joins those two boards with a check mark. The third room, unvisited, still has blank boards. Bright corridor lighting, methodical, puzzle-like mood. Labels: "NIL" on the crossed-out boards, "DECIDED" above the matching boards 3.
